Finer task division and a steady rhythm reduce waiting and walking; higher output spreads equipment costs across more cars ([[p:scale|economies of scale]]).
任何复杂的立体形状都能切成几千层薄片；每层只是一个二维图形，很容易用喷头或激光\: A complex solid shape can be divided into thousands of thin slices. Each slice is a two-dimensional shape that a nozzle or laser can draw; stacking the slices reconstructs the solid ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]). Instead of removing material by machining, the process adds it only where needed, hence the name additive manufacturing.
工业机器人是由多个关节串起来的机械臂；精确控制每个关节转多少度，末端的夹爪或焊枪: An industrial robot is an arm with several connected joints. Controlling how far each joint rotates places the gripper or welding torch at the required position and orientation ([[p:newton|Newtonian mechanics]]). Encoders at the joints continuously measure their actual angles so the controller can correct deviations ([[p:feedback|feedback and control]]).
火箭把推进剂烧成高温燃气，从喷管高速向后喷出；燃气获得向后的动量，火箭就获得同样: A rocket burns propellant into hot gas and ejects it backward at high speed through a nozzle. The gas gains backward momentum, while the rocket gains an equal amount of forward momentum ([[p:momentum|conservation of momentum]]). Because it carries its own oxidizer, it needs no air and works in a vacuum—a fundamental difference from an air-breathing jet engine.
火箭每喷出一点燃气就轻一点，后面的燃气推的是更轻的火箭。把这个过程累加起来，得到: As a rocket expels gas, it gets lighter, so later gas accelerates a lighter rocket. Adding up this process gives the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation: **change in rocket velocity = exhaust velocity × ln(initial mass ÷ mass after the propellant is burned)** ([[p:momentum|conservation of momentum]]). Velocity change grows only with the logarithm of the mass ratio, so gaining more speed demands a rapidly increasing amount of propellant ([[p:exponential|exponential growth]]).
一枚火箭的造价里，推进剂只占很小一部分（常不到 1%），贵的是发动机和箱体。用一: Propellant is only a small part of a rocket’s cost, often less than 1%; engines and tanks are expensive. Throwing them away after one launch is like discarding an airliner after each flight. Recovering and reusing the expensive first stage spreads its cost over multiple launches ([[p:scale|economies of scale and learning curves]]). The difficulty is that returning also needs propellant, and the rocket equation makes every extra kilogram costly ([[p:momentum|conservation of momentum]]).
水平扔出一块石头，它会落地；扔得越快，落得越远。如果快到约 7.9 公里/秒（*: Throw a stone horizontally and it falls to the ground; throw it faster and it travels farther before landing. At about 7.9 km/s—the **first cosmic velocity**—Earth’s surface curves away as quickly as the object falls, so it keeps falling around Earth without reaching the ground. That is an orbit ([[p:gravity|gravitation and orbits]], [[p:newton|Newton’s laws of motion]]). Astronauts feel weightless because they and their spacecraft are falling together, not because gravity has disappeared.
每颗导航卫星都在不停广播\"我是谁、我在哪、现在几点\"。接收机比较信号发出和收: Each navigation satellite continually broadcasts its identity, position and time. A receiver measures the delay between transmission and reception, then multiplies it by the speed of light to find its distance from the satellite. Distances from three satellites locate a point; because a phone’s clock is not accurate enough, a fourth satellite is needed to solve for the clock error. At least 4 satellites are therefore required ([[p:emwave|electromagnetic waves]]). A timing error of 1 microsecond means a distance error of 300 meters, so satellites carry atomic clocks (see [[atomic-clock]]).
从地球表面登上月球再回来，需要的速度增量远超任何单枚火箭的能力（[[p:mome: Traveling from Earth’s surface to the Moon and back requires a velocity change far beyond what a single rocket can provide directly ([[p:momentum|conservation of momentum]]). Apollo’s key choice was **lunar-orbit rendezvous**: a light lunar module descended to the surface while the main spacecraft waited in orbit. The lunar module then launched and docked with it for the return journey. Minimizing the mass taken to and from the surface made one Saturn V sufficient ([[p:gravity|gravitation and orbits]]).
经典计算机的 n 个比特在任一时刻只表示 2ⁿ 种状态中的一种；n 个量子比特却: At any instant, n classical bits represent just one of 2ⁿ possible states. In contrast, n qubits can be in a superposition of all those states, described by 2ⁿ probability amplitudes ([[p:superposition|superposition and entanglement]]). Measurement yields only one random result, so quantum computing is not simply calculating every answer at once. Carefully designed operations make amplitudes for wrong answers cancel and those for correct answers reinforce one another. Only certain problems, such as factoring large numbers and simulating molecules, have a suitable structure ([[p:complexity|computational complexity]]).
钢是含碳约 0.02%—2% 的铁合金。碳更少的熟铁软，碳更多（2%—4%）的铸: Steel is an iron alloy containing about 0.02–2% carbon. Wrought iron has less carbon and is soft; cast iron, with about 2–4% carbon, is hard and brittle. Heat treatment gives steel much of its versatility: rapidly cooling red-hot steel in water, or quenching, traps carbon in a hard structure called martensite. Subsequent tempering restores some toughness. Adding chromium, nickel, manganese and other elements produces thousands of steel grades.
今天主要有两条生产路线：**高炉—转炉**：[[blast-furnace|高炉: Today there are two main production routes. **Blast furnace–basic oxygen furnace**: a [[blast-furnace|blast furnace]] produces molten iron, then a [[basic-oxygen-steelmaking|basic oxygen furnace]] blows in oxygen to reduce its carbon content. **Scrap–electric arc furnace**: an [[electric-arc-furnace|electric arc furnace]] melts scrap steel in a shorter, lower-emission process. Finally, continuous casting and rolling produce steel plates, reinforcing bars and pipes.
氢气（今天主要从天然气或煤制取）和氮气（来自空气）按 3:1 混合，压缩到约 1: Hydrogen, now mainly produced from natural gas or coal, is mixed with nitrogen from air in a 3:1 ratio. The mixture is compressed to about 150–300 atmospheres and fed into a reactor containing an iron catalyst at roughly 400–500°C. Only a small fraction becomes ammonia on each pass. The ammonia is therefore condensed and separated, and the remaining gases are recycled through the reactor.
聚合主要有两种方式：**加聚**——带双键的单体（如乙烯）一个接一个连上去，瞬间: There are two main routes to polymers. **Addition polymerization** links double-bond-containing monomers, such as ethylene, into long chains. **Condensation polymerization** builds chains step by step, releasing a small molecule such as water each time monomers join; nylon and polyester are made this way.
按受热表现分：**热塑性塑料**链间无化学键，可反复熔化成型；**热固性塑料**: **Thermoplastics** have no chemical links between chains and can be melted and shaped repeatedly. **Thermosets** form cross-linked networks and do not melt again after curing. **Elastomers**, such as rubber, are lightly cross-linked and spring back after stretching. Cellulose, proteins and DNA are also natural polymers.
五种通用塑料占了产量的大头：**聚乙烯**（PE，塑料袋、薄膜、瓶子）、**聚丙: Five common plastics account for most production: **polyethylene** (PE: bags, films and bottles), **polypropylene** (PP: food containers and car bumpers), **polyvinyl chloride** (PVC: pipes and flooring), **polyethylene terephthalate** (PET: drink bottles and polyester fibers), and **polystyrene** (PS: foam packaging). Their raw materials come from [[petrochemicals|petrochemicals]]; after additives are mixed in, processes such as [[injection-molding|injection molding]] shape the products.
工业革命不是一项发明，而是一连串互相\"催促\"的创新：纺纱快了，织布成了瓶颈，: The Industrial Revolution was a chain of innovations that prompted further innovations. Faster spinning made weaving the bottleneck, encouraging power looms. More machines required more iron and coal. Mines needed drainage, encouraging steam engines, which then powered factories, ships and trains.
英国率先发生，因为几个条件凑在一起：煤多易采，工资高而能源便宜（用机器替人划算）: Britain led because several conditions came together: abundant, accessible coal; high wages and cheap energy that made replacing labor with machines worthwhile; patent protection for inventors; colonial trade supplying cotton and markets; and many skilled craftspeople.
前提是 [[interchangeable-parts|可互换零件]]：零件直接: The prerequisite is [[interchangeable-parts|interchangeable parts]] that fit without hand adjustment. Engineers divide assembly into tens or hundreds of operations, time them and balance workloads so that every station follows the same rhythm. Conveyors deliver parts to each station when needed.
福特先在磁电机装配上试验：拆成 29 道工序后，每件用时从约 20 分钟降到约: Ford first experimented with magneto assembly. Dividing the work into 29 operations reduced the time per unit from about 20 minutes to about 5 minutes.
[[cad-cam|CAD]] 模型经切片软件切成薄层。主要工艺：**熔融沉积（: Slicing software divides a [[cad-cam|CAD]] model into thin layers. Main processes include **fused deposition modeling (FDM)**, which extrudes molten plastic filament like toothpaste and is the cheapest method; **stereolithography (SLA)**, which uses ultraviolet light to cure liquid resin layer by layer, producing smooth surfaces useful in dentistry; and **powder-bed fusion (SLS/SLM)**, which uses a laser to fuse successive powder layers and can produce metal parts.
优势是无需模具、形状几乎不受限制，适合原型和定制；缺点是慢，大批量时比 [[in: It needs no mold and allows almost unrestricted shapes, making it useful for prototypes and customized products. The disadvantages are slow production and higher costs than [[injection-molding|injection molding]] at large volumes.
最常见的是六轴关节机器人：前三个轴决定手腕到达哪里，后三个轴决定工具朝向哪个方向: The most common design is a six-axis articulated robot. The first three axes position the wrist, while the last three orient the tool. Joints are driven by [[servo-motor|servo motors]] and precision gear reducers. An engineer teaches a path with a handheld controller or programs it offline; the robot then repeats it day and night with repeatability of a fraction of a millimeter.
传统机器人力大速快，须用围栏与人隔开；后来有了 [[cobot|协作机器人]]，: Traditional industrial robots are strong and fast, so fences separate them from people. Later developments include [[cobot|collaborative robots]] and [[machine-vision|machine vision]] for recognizing parts.
一枚运载火箭的绝大部分质量是推进剂，结构和有效载荷只占一小部分。燃烧室里的高压燃: Most of a launch rocket’s mass is propellant; structure and payload account for only a small fraction. High-pressure combustion gases pass through a converging–diverging de Laval nozzle, accelerating to 2.5–4.5 km/s. Thrust equals mass expelled per second multiplied by exhaust velocity. The rocket also controls its attitude by swiveling engines or firing small gas jets. A programmed maneuver gradually flattens its trajectory until it gains the horizontal speed needed for orbit (see [[orbit]]).
从地面进入近地轨道，算上空气阻力和重力损失，大约需要 9.4 公里/秒的速度增量: Reaching low Earth orbit from the ground requires about 9.4 km/s of velocity change, including drag and gravity losses. Even efficient liquid hydrogen–oxygen propulsion, with an exhaust velocity near 4.4 km/s, needs a mass ratio close to 9. Of 100 tonnes at launch, about 89 tonnes are propellant; the remaining 11 tonnes must include tanks, engines and payload. This is why payload is often only 2–4% of launch mass. Engineers can increase exhaust velocity through better propellants or [[ion-thruster]], reduce structural mass, and discard empty stages (see [[multistage-rocket]]).
以猎鹰 9 号为例：一二级分离后，第一级翻转调头，发动机点火减速；穿过大气时用栅: For Falcon 9, after stage separation the first stage turns around and fires its engines to slow down. Grid fins steer it through the atmosphere, and another burn during reentry reduces heating. A final retropropulsive burn and deployed landing legs bring it down near the launch site or on an uncrewed ship at sea. Automatic guidance continually corrects the flight ([[p:feedback|feedback and control]]). Reserving propellant for recovery reduces payload capacity by roughly 30% compared with expendable use.
轨道越高，需要的速度越慢、绕一圈的时间越长：约 400 公里高的空间站约 90: Higher orbits require lower speeds and take longer to complete. A space station about 400 km high circles Earth in roughly 90 minutes; a geostationary orbit about 36,000 km high takes one day (see [[geostationary-orbit]]). A speed of 11.2 km/s, the **second cosmic velocity**, allows escape from Earth; 16.7 km/s, the **third cosmic velocity**, allows escape from the Solar System. To change orbital height, an engine burn must occur at the right point: accelerating forward raises the opposite side of the orbit.
GPS 卫星在约 2 万公里高的中轨道上运行。它们跑得快，按狭义相对论时钟每天慢: GPS satellites orbit about 20,000 km above Earth. Their speed makes their clocks run about 7 microseconds slower per day under special relativity, while weaker gravity makes them run about 45 microseconds faster under general relativity. The net effect is about 38 microseconds faster per day ([[p:relativity|relativistic effects]]). Without correction, position errors would accumulate by roughly 10 km per day. Ordinary phones locate themselves to within a few meters; corrections from ground reference stations, using techniques such as RTK, can provide centimeter-level accuracy for surveying, automated farm machinery and drones.
土星五号高 110 米，三级火箭把飞船送往月球。飞船由三部分组成：**指令舱**: The Saturn V stood 110 meters tall and used three stages to send the spacecraft toward the Moon. The spacecraft had three parts: the **command module**, the only part that returned to Earth; the **service module**, with the engine and power supply; and the **lunar module**, whose descent stage stayed on the surface as a launch platform while the ascent stage returned two astronauts to orbit. The round trip took about 8 days, supported by a ground tracking network and an Apollo Guidance Computer with about 4 KB of memory.
① 量子比特：用超导电路、被囚禁的离子或中性原子等物理系统实现。: ① Qubits: implemented using physical systems such as superconducting circuits, trapped ions or neutral atoms.
② 量子门：用精确控制的微波或激光脉冲操纵量子比特的状态，把它们纠缠起来。: ② Quantum gates: precisely controlled microwave or laser pulses manipulate qubit states and entangle the qubits.
③ 纠错：噪声会很快破坏量子态，需要 [[quantum-error-corre: ③ Error correction: noise quickly damages quantum states, so [[quantum-error-correction|quantum error correction]] encodes one reliable logical qubit using many physical qubits.
\"钢\"和\"铁\"在日常话里常混用，但材料学上二者差别正是那一点点碳。: Steel and iron are often used interchangeably in everyday speech, but in materials science that small amount of carbon is the key distinction.
哈伯—博施法本身并不\"创造\"能量，它是用大量化石能源换取了作物能直接吸收的氮: The Haber–Bosch process does not create energy. It uses substantial amounts of fossil energy to produce nitrogen compounds that crops can absorb.
塑料瓶底的三角形数字（1—7）是材料种类标识，不代表\"可以回收\"。: The number from 1 to 7 inside a triangle on a plastic bottle identifies its material. It does not mean the bottle is recyclable.
\"工业革命\"持续了近一个世纪，增长起初很缓慢，并非一夜之间的剧变。: The Industrial Revolution lasted almost a century. Growth was slow at first, rather than an overnight transformation.
福特并没有发明流水线的每个要素，他的贡献是把可互换零件、专用机床、传送带和工序分: Ford did not invent every element of the assembly line. His contribution was combining interchangeable parts, specialized machine tools, conveyors and task division into a complete system.
3D 打印曾被宣传为会让\"每家每户成为工厂\"，实际上它主要是对传统制造的补充: 3D printing was once promoted as a way to turn every home into a factory. In practice, it mostly complements traditional manufacturing rather than replacing it.
用量子比特的叠加和纠缠并行探索大量可能，对特定问题可能指数级加速。: Uses qubit superposition and entanglement to explore many possibilities, potentially giving exponential speedups for particular problems.
1981 年，费曼（Richard Feynman）提出用量子系统来模拟量子世界: In 1981, Richard Feynman proposed using quantum systems to simulate the quantum world. In 1994, [[shor-algorithm|Shor’s algorithm]] showed that quantum computation could break RSA. Google announced quantum supremacy in 2019. In December 2024, its Willow chip demonstrated error correction in which adding more qubits reduced the logical error rate. The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics recognized macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, the basis of superconducting qubits.
目前的量子计算机只有几十到一千多个带噪声的物理比特，尚不能解决有实际价值的问题；: Current quantum computers have tens to more than a thousand noisy physical qubits and cannot yet solve practically valuable problems. Nevertheless, they have already prompted worldwide changes to cryptography (see [[post-quantum-crypto|post-quantum cryptography]]). Possible applications include drug discovery, materials and chemical simulation.
经典比特与量子比特：经典比特非 0 即 1；量子比特可以是两者的叠加，测量时按概: Classical bits and qubits: a classical bit is either 0 or 1, while a qubit can be a superposition of both and collapses probabilistically when measured. Describing n qubits requires 2ⁿ numbers. Quantum computation uses interference to reinforce the probability amplitudes of correct answers.
可以同时处于 0 和 1 叠加态的信息单元，可由超导电路、离子、光子等实现。: An information unit that can be in a superposition of 0 and 1, implemented using superconducting circuits, ions, photons or other systems.
量子比特是一个有两个基本状态的量子系统，记作 |0⟩ 和 |1⟩。它可以处于两者: A qubit is a quantum system with two basis states, written |0⟩ and |1⟩. It can occupy a superposition α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, yielding 0 with probability |α|² and 1 with probability |β|² when measured ([[p:superposition|superposition]]). Qubits can also be entangled: even when far apart, measuring one immediately changes predictions for the other’s result.
超导量子比特是芯片上的微型电路，利用约瑟夫森结让电路的能级不再等间距，挑出最低的: A superconducting qubit is a tiny circuit on a chip. A Josephson junction makes its energy levels unevenly spaced, allowing the lowest two to serve as 0 and 1. Ion traps suspend individual ions using electromagnetic fields and use two atomic energy levels. Photonic qubits encode information in a photon’s polarization or path. The time a superposition lasts is its coherence time, a key quality measure that must be much longer than a gate operation.
20 世纪 90 年代，物理学家舒马赫（Benjamin Schumacher）: In the 1990s, physicist Benjamin Schumacher introduced the term “qubit.” From 1995 onward, ion-trap and nuclear-magnetic-resonance experiments demonstrated the first quantum logic gates.
量子比特把信息的基本单位从\"非此即彼\"扩展到\"概率幅\"，成为量子计算、量: Qubits extend the basic unit of information from an either/or choice to probability amplitudes, providing a common language for quantum computing, communication and sensing.
能在量子计算机上高效分解大整数，理论上可破解今天的 RSA 加密。: Efficiently factors large integers on a quantum computer and could, in theory, break today’s RSA encryption.
RSA 的安全性依赖于大数难以分解（[[p:oneway|单向函数]]）。秀尔发: RSA security relies on the difficulty of factoring large numbers ([[p:oneway|one-way functions]]). Shor discovered that factoring can be transformed into finding the period of a sequence. Superposition and the quantum Fourier transform let a quantum computer find that period efficiently ([[p:superposition|superposition]]).
先让量子寄存器处于所有输入的叠加态；再做量子傅里叶变换，让与周期相关的结果概率大: First, a quantum register is put into a superposition of inputs. A quantum Fourier transform then boosts the probabilities of results associated with the period. After measurement, a classical computer uses the period to derive the factors.
1994 年，美国数学家秀尔（Peter Shor）提出这一算法；2001 年，: American mathematician Peter Shor proposed the algorithm in 1994. In 2001, IBM demonstrated factoring 15 = 3 × 5 on a nuclear-magnetic-resonance quantum computer.
破解实际使用的 RSA 需要大量纠错后的逻辑比特，目前远未实现；但\"先截获、以: Breaking RSA as used in practice requires many error-corrected logical qubits, which remain far beyond current capabilities. But the threat of collecting encrypted data now and decrypting it later has already prompted countries to migrate to post-quantum cryptography.
超导、离子阱、中性原子、光量子、拓扑等路线各有长短，尚无定论。: Superconducting circuits, trapped ions, neutral atoms, photons and topological approaches each have advantages and disadvantages; no winner has emerged.
任何能被精确控制、又能与环境隔离的两能级量子系统都可以做量子比特（[[p:sup: Any precisely controllable two-level quantum system that can be isolated from its environment can serve as a qubit ([[p:superposition|superposition]]). Different physical systems trade off speed, accuracy and scalability, so several approaches coexist.
超导路线用芯片工艺制造，速度快，但需要约 10 毫开的极低温；离子阱的精度最高、: Superconducting qubits use chip-manufacturing techniques and operate quickly, but need temperatures near 10 millikelvin. Trapped ions offer very high accuracy and flexible connections between qubits, but operations are slower. Neutral-atom systems arrange thousands or tens of thousands of atoms with optical tweezers and scale well. Photonic systems operate at room temperature. Topological approaches aim for inherent resistance to noise.
谷歌、IBM 和中国科学技术大学等主要走超导路线；2025 年 2 月微软发布基: Google, IBM and the University of Science and Technology of China are among those pursuing superconducting systems. In February 2025, Microsoft announced Majorana 1, a chip based on topological principles. However, Nature’s editorial note stated that the accompanying paper did not provide evidence for Majorana zero modes, and the claim remains disputed.
最终可能由工程上的可扩展性决定胜负。: Engineering scalability may ultimately determine which approach succeeds.
用许多物理比特编码一个更可靠的逻辑比特，是实用量子计算机的必经之路。: Encodes one more reliable logical qubit using many physical qubits, a necessary step toward useful quantum computers.
经典纠错可以简单地复制比特，但量子态无法被复制，而且直接测量会破坏它。量子纠错的: Classical error correction can copy bits, but an unknown quantum state cannot be copied, and direct measurement disrupts it. Quantum error correction spreads a logical qubit’s information across the entangled states of many physical qubits ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]). Measuring only relationships between qubits reveals errors so they can be corrected.
最受关注的表面码把物理比特排成二维网格，一部分反复检查相邻比特，经典计算机据此推: The widely studied surface code arranges physical qubits in a two-dimensional grid. Some repeatedly check their neighbors, allowing a classical computer to infer where errors occurred. Adding qubits reduces the logical error rate only when the physical error rate is below a threshold.
1995 年，秀尔提出了第一个量子纠错码；2024 年，谷歌 Willow 芯片: Shor proposed the first quantum error-correcting code in 1995. In 2024, Google’s Willow chip demonstrated below-threshold error correction in which larger codes performed better.
据估计，一个有用的逻辑比特可能需要成百上千个物理比特。: Estimates suggest that one useful logical qubit may require hundreds or thousands of physical qubits.
量子计算机在某个特定任务上明显超越最强经典计算机的里程碑。: A milestone in which a quantum computer clearly outperforms the strongest classical computer on a specific task.
要证明量子计算机真的有用，首先得找一个任务，让它比最强的经典超级计算机快得多（[: To demonstrate quantum computing’s potential, researchers first seek a task it can perform much faster than the strongest classical supercomputer ([[p:complexity|computational complexity]]). These tasks are often specially designed, such as sampling outputs from random quantum circuits.
让量子芯片运行随机线路并采集样本；经典一方则用超算和最好的算法尝试完成同样的任务: A quantum chip runs random circuits and collects samples. Classical researchers then use supercomputers and their best algorithms to attempt the same task.
2019 年，谷歌用 53 个比特的\"悬铃木\"处理器宣称 200 秒完成了超: In 2019, Google claimed its 53-qubit Sycamore processor had completed in 200 seconds a task that would take a supercomputer 10,000 years. IBM immediately argued that better classical methods could be much faster. In 2020, the University of Science and Technology of China announced quantum supremacy in another sampling task using Jiuzhang.
这是量子计算的里程碑，但这些任务本身没有实用价值；经典算法也在不断改进。: This is a milestone for quantum computing, but the tasks themselves have no practical value, and classical algorithms continue to improve.
用单光子的量子态分发密钥，任何窃听都会留下痕迹；中国\"墨子号\"卫星实现了星地: Distributes keys using the quantum states of individual photons, so eavesdropping leaves traces. China’s Micius satellite demonstrated satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution.
量子力学规定，未知的量子态不能被完美复制，测量会不可避免地扰动它（[[p:sup: Quantum mechanics prevents perfect copying of an unknown quantum state, and measurement inevitably disturbs it ([[p:superposition|superposition and measurement]]). When single-photon polarization carries a key, interception introduces errors. Comparing part of their data allows sender and receiver to detect eavesdropping.
在 BB84 协议中，发送方随机选择两组偏振方向之一来编码每个比特，接收方也随机: In BB84, the sender randomly chooses one of two polarization bases to encode each bit, while the receiver randomly chooses a basis for measurement. They later announce their chosen bases publicly and keep only bits for which the choices match. They test a sample of these bits; an unusually high error rate indicates eavesdropping, so that key is discarded.
1984 年，贝内特（Charles Bennett）和布拉萨德（Gilles: Charles Bennett and Gilles Brassard proposed BB84 in 1984. China launched the Micius quantum-science satellite in 2016 and demonstrated satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution over more than a thousand kilometers in 2017.
量子密钥分发提供了基于物理定律而非计算难度的安全性；但光子在光纤中会衰减，远距离: Quantum key distribution bases security on physical laws rather than computational difficulty. However, photons weaken in optical fibers, and long-distance links require trusted relays, so many security agencies prefer to promote post-quantum cryptography.
BB84 量子密钥分发：双方各自随机选择测量方式，事后公开比对，只保留方式一致的: BB84 quantum key distribution: sender and receiver randomly choose their measurement bases, compare those choices publicly afterward, and keep matching bits for a key. An eavesdropper’s measurements introduce detectable errors.
利用量子态对外界极其敏感的特点，测量磁场、重力、时间达到前所未有的精度。: Uses the extreme sensitivity of quantum states to measure magnetic fields, gravity and time with unprecedented precision.
量子态对外界的磁场、电场、重力和温度极其敏感，这在计算中是麻烦，在测量中却是优点: Quantum states are extremely sensitive to magnetic and electric fields, gravity and temperature. This is a problem for computing but an advantage for sensing ([[p:levels|energy levels]], [[p:superposition|superposition]]). Small external changes alter energy-level spacings or a superposition’s phase; measuring that change reveals the external physical quantity.
原子钟以原子跃迁频率为基准；原子干涉仪让原子同时走两条路径再汇合，从干涉条纹中读: Atomic clocks use atomic transition frequencies as references. Atom interferometers send atoms along two paths that later recombine, extracting gravitational acceleration from the interference pattern. Nitrogen-vacancy defects in diamond measure nanoscale magnetic fields at room temperature.
原子钟是最早的量子传感器（1955 年）。: Atomic clocks, introduced in 1955, were the earliest quantum sensors.
量子传感用于不依赖卫星的导航、脑磁成像和基础物理检验，是量子技术中最接近实用的方: Quantum sensing supports satellite-independent navigation, magnetic imaging of the brain and tests of fundamental physics. It is among the quantum technologies closest to practical use.
能抵抗量子计算机攻击的新型公钥算法，美国 NIST 于 2024 年发布首批标准: New public-key algorithms designed to resist quantum-computer attacks; the US NIST published the first standards in 2024.
Shor 算法能破解基于大数分解和离散对数的公钥密码，但并非所有数学难题都怕量子: Shor’s algorithm breaks public-key cryptography based on factoring or discrete logarithms, but not every mathematical problem is vulnerable to quantum computers. No efficient classical or quantum algorithms are currently known for the relevant lattice problems ([[p:oneway|one-way functions]]), making them a basis for new public-key cryptography.
新算法和现有的公钥密码用法相同：密钥交换和数字签名，只是数学基础不同，密钥和签名: The new algorithms perform the same jobs as existing public-key systems—key exchange and digital signatures—but use different mathematics and usually have larger keys and signatures. During migration, hybrid systems commonly combine traditional and post-quantum algorithms.
2016 年，美国国家标准与技术研究院（NIST）发起公开征集；2024 年 8: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology, NIST, launched an open call in 2016. In August 2024, it published its first three standards, including lattice-based ML-KEM, formerly Kyber, and ML-DSA.
主流浏览器已开始部署后量子密钥交换。: Major browsers have begun deploying post-quantum key exchange.
用一个可控的量子系统去模拟另一个难以计算的量子系统，这正是费曼提出量子计算的初衷: Uses a controllable quantum system to simulate another quantum system that is difficult to calculate, following Feynman’s original motivation for quantum computing.
描述 n 个相互作用的量子粒子需要的数字数量随 n 指数增长，经典计算机很快就算: The number of values needed to describe n interacting quantum particles grows exponentially with n, quickly overwhelming classical computers ([[p:complexity|computational complexity]]). Feynman’s idea was to let an easily controlled quantum system imitate the difficult system instead of calculating everything classically ([[p:superposition|superposition]]).
模拟量子计算机用冷原子、离子或超导电路搭建一个\"人造材料\"，让它的相互作用与: An analog quantum simulator builds an artificial material from cold atoms, ions or superconducting circuits, arranging its interactions to match the system under study.
1982 年，费曼在论文《用计算机模拟物理》中提出这一设想；2002 年，实验物: Feynman set out the idea in his 1982 paper Simulating Physics with Computers. In 2002, experimental physicists observed a transition from a superfluid to an insulator using cold atoms in an optical lattice.
它被认为是量子计算最早可能产生科学价值的应用，目标包括高温超导的机理和新药分子的: It is considered one of the earliest potentially valuable scientific applications of quantum computing, with goals including understanding high-temperature superconductivity and designing drug molecules.
某些材料冷却到临界温度以下电阻完全消失，可制造强磁体和量子比特。: Some materials lose all electrical resistance below a critical temperature, enabling powerful magnets and qubits.
在普通导体中，电子不断被晶格振动和杂质散射。某些材料在冷却到临界温度以下时，电子: In ordinary conductors, electrons scatter from lattice vibrations and impurities. Below a critical temperature in certain materials, electrons form Cooper pairs, which condense into a common quantum state and no longer scatter in the same way ([[p:superposition|macroscopic quantum states]]). Electrical resistance becomes exactly zero. Superconductors also expel internal magnetic fields, known as the Meissner effect.
超导线圈一旦通电，电流可以在没有电源的情况下流动多年，产生强大而稳定的磁场。核磁: Once current is established in a superconducting coil, it can flow for years without a power supply, producing a strong, stable magnetic field. Powerful magnets in MRI scanners, particle accelerators and tokamaks use superconducting wire such as niobium-titanium.
1911 年，荷兰物理学家昂内斯（Heike Kamerlingh Onnes）: In 1911, Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered superconductivity in mercury cooled with liquid helium. The Meissner effect was discovered in 1933. In 1957, Bardeen, Cooper and Schrieffer proposed BCS theory to explain superconductivity, earning the 1972 Nobel Prize in Physics.
超导磁体让 [[mri|核磁共振成像]]走进医院，让大型强子对撞机能弯转接近光速: Superconducting magnets brought [[mri|MRI]] into hospitals, allow the Large Hadron Collider to bend the paths of near-light-speed protons, and make superconducting magnetic-levitation trains possible.
超导的两个标志：降到临界温度以下，电阻突然变为零；磁场被排出超导体之外（迈斯纳效: Two signatures of superconductivity: resistance drops to zero below a critical temperature, and magnetic fields are expelled through the Meissner effect, allowing a magnet to levitate above a superconductor.
用电场把粒子加速到接近光速再撞击，探索物质最深层结构，也用于医疗和芯片。: Accelerates particles toward the speed of light using electric fields, then collides them to probe matter’s deepest structure. Accelerators also serve medicine and chip manufacturing.
带电粒子在电场中被加速，在磁场中被弯转（[[p:lorentz|洛伦兹力]]）。: Electric fields accelerate charged particles, while magnetic fields bend their paths ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]). Near the speed of light, additional energy produces little further increase in speed ([[p:relativity|relativity]]). Colliding these high-energy particles can convert energy into new particles, revealing matter’s fundamental structure.
直线加速器让粒子穿过一连串射频腔，每经过一个就被\"推\"一下；环形加速器用磁铁: A linear accelerator sends particles through successive radio-frequency cavities, each providing a push. A circular accelerator uses magnets to guide particles around a ring, accelerating them on each lap while increasing the magnetic field with their energy. In the Large Hadron Collider, two proton beams travel in opposite directions around a 27 km ring and collide inside detectors.
1931 年，美国物理学家劳伦斯（Ernest Lawrence）造出第一台回旋: Ernest Lawrence built the first cyclotron in 1931. In 1932, Cockcroft and Walton used accelerated protons to split an atomic nucleus artificially for the first time. CERN’s Large Hadron Collider discovered the Higgs boson in 2012.
加速器揭示了夸克和标准模型；全世界数万台加速器中，大部分用于医院的放射治疗、芯片: Accelerators helped reveal quarks and the Standard Model. Of the tens of thousands worldwide, most are used for hospital radiotherapy, ion implantation in chip manufacturing and industrial irradiation rather than basic research.
电子在环形加速器中转弯时发出极亮的 X 光，用于看清材料和蛋白质结构。: Electrons turning in a circular accelerator emit extremely bright X-rays, which reveal the structures of materials and proteins.
带电粒子做加速运动时会辐射电磁波（[[p:emwave|电磁波]]）。接近光速的: Accelerating charged particles emit electromagnetic radiation ([[p:emwave|electromagnetic waves]]). When near-light-speed electrons bend in a magnetic field ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]), they emit an intense, tightly directed beam of light along the tangent.
电子在储存环中以接近光速运行，经过弯转磁铁和交替排列的波荡器时发出强光，光沿几十: Electrons circulate near light speed in a storage ring, emitting intense light as they pass bending magnets and alternating arrays of magnets called undulators. Dozens of beamlines carry this light to experimental stations.
1947 年，美国通用电气公司的研究人员在同步加速器上首次观察到这种光；中国的上: General Electric researchers in the United States first observed this light in a synchrotron in 1947. The Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility opened in 2009; Beijing’s High Energy Photon Source represents a newer generation.
同步辐射成为解析蛋白质结构、研究电池材料和芯片缺陷的利器，蛋白质数据库中的大部分: Synchrotron radiation is a powerful tool for determining protein structures and studying battery materials and chip defects. It has determined most structures in the Protein Data Bank.
用数公里长的激光干涉仪测出比质子还小千倍的长度变化，2015 年首次直接探测到引: Kilometer-scale laser interferometers measure length changes about a thousand times smaller than a proton. Gravitational waves were first detected directly in 2015.
广义相对论预言，大质量天体剧烈运动时，会让时空本身产生涟漪（[[p:relati: General relativity predicts that violent motion of massive objects sends ripples through spacetime ([[p:relativity|relativity]]). A passing gravitational wave slightly stretches distances in one direction and compresses them in the perpendicular direction. Laser interference measures the difference between two long perpendicular arms to detect it ([[p:wave|interference]]).
LIGO 的两条真空臂各长 4 公里，激光往返后合在一起干涉。引力波造成的长度变: LIGO has two vacuum arms, each 4 km long. Laser light makes a round trip in each before recombining and interfering. Gravitational waves change their lengths by only about one-thousandth of a proton’s diameter, requiring exceptional noise isolation and confirmation by two widely separated detectors.
2015 年 9 月 14 日，美国 LIGO 首次直接探测到两个黑洞合并产生的: On September 14, 2015, the US LIGO detectors made the first direct detection of gravitational waves, from two merging black holes. Weiss, Barish and Thorne received the 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics.
人类有了观察宇宙的新\"感官\"，能\"听到\"黑洞和中子星的合并。: Humanity gained a new sense for observing the universe, allowing us to “hear” black holes and neutron stars merge.
铜氧化物等材料在液氮温度以上就能超导，让超导磁体和电缆的冷却便宜得多。: Materials such as copper oxides can superconduct above liquid-nitrogen temperature, greatly reducing the cooling cost of superconducting magnets and cables.
传统超导体需要液氦冷却。某些层状的铜氧化物陶瓷在更高的温度下就能超导，其临界温度: Conventional superconductors require liquid helium cooling. Some layered copper-oxide ceramics superconduct at temperatures above liquid nitrogen’s boiling point, −196°C ([[p:band|band structure]], [[p:structure|crystal structure]]). Liquid nitrogen is much cheaper than liquid helium.
这类材料由导电的铜氧平面和起\"储电荷\"作用的其他原子层交替堆叠而成，超导发生: These materials alternate conducting copper-oxygen planes with other atomic layers that act as charge reservoirs. Superconductivity occurs in the copper-oxygen planes. As brittle ceramics, they are difficult to turn into wires.
1986 年，IBM 苏黎世实验室的贝德诺尔茨和米勒发现镧钡铜氧化物在约 35: In 1986, Bednorz and Müller at IBM’s Zurich laboratory discovered superconductivity near 35 K in lanthanum-barium copper oxide. In 1987, Paul Chu and colleagues found it at 93 K in yttrium-barium copper oxide, exceeding liquid-nitrogen temperature for the first time.
高温超导带材正用于电缆和紧凑型核聚变装置的强磁体；但其超导机理至今没有公认的解释: High-temperature superconducting tapes are being used in cables and powerful magnets for compact fusion devices. Their superconducting mechanism still lacks a generally accepted explanation.
用激光把原子减速到接近绝对零度；1995 年首次实现玻色—爱因斯坦凝聚，是原子钟: Lasers slow atoms to temperatures near absolute zero. Bose–Einstein condensation was first achieved in 1995; cold atoms underpin atomic clocks and neutral-atom quantum computing.
原子迎着激光运动时，由于多普勒效应，会更容易吸收迎面而来的光子；每吸收一个光子，: An atom moving toward a laser beam is more likely to absorb an approaching photon because of the Doppler effect. Each absorbed photon gives it a small slowing kick ([[p:momentum|momentum]]). Surrounding atoms with several laser beams can cool them to around a millionth of a kelvin ([[p:levels|energy levels]]).
先用激光冷却和磁场囚禁原子，再\"蒸发\"掉速度最快的原子，进一步降温到十亿分之: Atoms are first laser-cooled and trapped using magnetic fields. The fastest atoms are then allowed to evaporate away, cooling the rest to the nanokelvin range. Many atoms occupy a common quantum state, forming a Bose–Einstein condensate.
1997 年，朱棣文、科恩-唐努德日和菲利普斯因激光冷却获诺贝尔物理学奖；199: Steven Chu, Claude Cohen-Tannoudji and William Phillips received the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics for laser cooling. Cornell, Wieman and Ketterle first achieved Bose–Einstein condensation in 1995.
冷原子是最精确的原子钟、原子干涉重力仪和中性原子量子计算机的基础。: Cold atoms underpin the most precise atomic clocks, atom-interferometer gravimeters and neutral-atom quantum computers.
啁啾脉冲放大让激光脉冲又短又强，阿秒脉冲短到能\"拍下\"电子的运动。: Chirped-pulse amplification produces short, powerful laser pulses. Attosecond pulses are brief enough to capture electron motion.
激光脉冲越短，越能\"冻结\"快速的过程；但直接放大极短的强脉冲会烧毁光学元件。: Shorter laser pulses can freeze faster processes, but directly amplifying an intense ultrashort pulse damages optical components. The solution is to stretch the pulse in time to reduce peak power, amplify it, then compress it again ([[p:wave|waves and spectra]]). This is chirped-pulse amplification.
飞秒激光的脉冲只有千万亿分之一秒量级；把它聚焦到气体中，可以产生更短的阿秒（10: Femtosecond laser pulses last on the order of 10⁻¹⁵ seconds. Focusing them into a gas can generate even shorter attosecond pulses, around 10⁻¹⁸ seconds, for observing electron motion in atoms.
1985 年，穆鲁（Gérard Mourou）和斯特里克兰（Donna Str: Gérard Mourou and Donna Strickland invented chirped-pulse amplification in 1985 and received the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physics. Agostini, Krausz and L’Huillier received the 2023 prize for attosecond light pulses.
超快激光被用于近视矫正手术、精密加工，以及超快过程研究。: Ultrafast lasers are used in vision-correction surgery, precision manufacturing and research on ultrafast processes.
模仿大脑神经元和突触的芯片，用\"脉冲\"传递信息，追求极低功耗。: Chips inspired by neurons and synapses use spikes to communicate, aiming for extremely low power consumption.
人脑约有 860 亿个神经元，功耗只有约 20 瓦；它不分\"处理器\"和\"内: The human brain has about 86 billion neurons yet consumes only about 20 watts. It has no separate processor and memory; computation and storage are distributed through the same network, and neurons send spikes in response to events ([[p:division|division of labor and parallelism]]). Imitating this architecture can greatly reduce power consumption.
类脑芯片集成大量人工神经元和突触电路，用异步的脉冲事件传递信息，突触权重就存在计: Neuromorphic chips contain many artificial neuron and synapse circuits. They communicate through asynchronous spike events, with synaptic weights stored next to the computing elements. Without spikes, circuits consume almost no power. Algorithms for spiking neural networks are still developing.
20 世纪 80 年代，加州理工学院的米德（Carver Mead）提出\"神经: Caltech’s Carver Mead proposed neuromorphic engineering in the 1980s. IBM released TrueNorth in 2014, and Intel introduced Loihi in 2017.
它在传感器边缘处理等低功耗场景展现了潜力；但目前主流 AI 仍运行在 GPU 等: Neuromorphic computing shows promise in low-power applications such as processing sensor data at the edge. Mainstream AI still runs on GPUs and other conventional architectures, and neuromorphic computing has yet to find its defining application.
用光代替电在芯片内外传输甚至计算数据，速度快、发热少。: Uses light instead of electricity to transmit—and potentially compute—data inside and between chips, offering high speed and less heat.
电信号在铜线中传输会发热、损耗大，带宽受限；光在波导中传输几乎不发热（[[p:o: Electrical signals in copper wires produce heat, suffer losses and face bandwidth limits. Light passing through waveguides produces almost no heat ([[p:optics|optics]]). Optical interference can naturally perform matrix multiplication, prompting efforts to compute directly with light.
硅光技术用成熟的芯片工艺，在硅片上制作光波导、调制器和探测器，把电信号转换成光信: Silicon photonics uses established chip processes to build optical waveguides, modulators and detectors on silicon, converting electrical signals into light for transmission and reception. Many data-center optical modules already use it. Optical computing uses interferometer arrays for neural-network matrix operations.
2000 年代起，英特尔等公司大力研发硅光技术；2010 年代后期起，硅光模块在: Intel and other companies invested heavily in silicon photonics from the 2000s onward. Large-scale deployment of silicon-photonic modules in data centers began in the late 2010s.
AI 集群对带宽的需求让光互连成为关键技术；全光计算仍面临非线性运算困难、精度有: AI clusters’ bandwidth demands make optical interconnects increasingly important. Fully optical computing still faces difficulties with nonlinear operations and limited precision.
利用电子的自旋而非电荷存储信息；巨磁阻效应让硬盘容量暴增。: Stores information using electron spin rather than charge. Giant magnetoresistance dramatically increased hard-drive capacity.
电子除了带电荷，还有一种量子属性叫自旋（[[p:levels|量子属性]]）。在: Electrons have a quantum property called spin in addition to electric charge ([[p:levels|quantum properties]]). In magnetic multilayer films, their ease of passage depends on the alignment of their spins with each layer’s magnetization. Resistance therefore changes strongly with an applied magnetic field: giant magnetoresistance.
硬盘读头由两层磁性薄膜夹着一层极薄的非磁性层构成，一层固定、一层随盘片磁信号翻转: A hard-drive read head has two magnetic films separated by a very thin nonmagnetic layer. One magnetic layer is fixed, while the other responds to the disk’s magnetic signal. Parallel magnetizations give lower resistance; opposite magnetizations give higher resistance, allowing the head to read 0s and 1s.
1988 年，费尔（Albert Fert）和格林贝格尔（Peter Grünb: Albert Fert and Peter Grünberg independently discovered giant magnetoresistance in 1988 and received the 2007 Nobel Prize in Physics.
硬盘能读出越来越小的磁信号，容量在十几年里增长了上千倍；自旋电子学还催生了 [[: Reading ever smaller magnetic signals allowed hard-drive capacity to rise more than a thousandfold over a little more than a decade. Spintronics also led to [[mram|magnetoresistive memory]].
用磁性隧道结存数据的非易失内存，速度接近 DRAM。: Nonvolatile memory that stores data in magnetic tunnel junctions, with speeds approaching DRAM.
磁性隧道结由两层磁性薄膜夹着一层只有几个原子厚的绝缘层组成，电子以隧穿的方式穿过: A magnetic tunnel junction has two magnetic films separated by an insulating layer only a few atoms thick. Electrons cross the insulator by tunneling ([[p:tunneling|quantum tunneling]]). Parallel magnetizations give low resistance and opposite magnetizations high resistance, representing 0 and 1. The magnetizations persist after power is removed.
写入时用电流产生的磁场，或者让自旋极化的电流直接\"扭转\"自由层的磁化方向；读: Writing uses either a current-generated magnetic field or a spin-polarized current that directly twists the free layer’s magnetization. Reading measures resistance. MRAM aims to combine DRAM-like speed and nearly unlimited rewriting with flash-like retention without power.
2006 年，飞思卡尔公司推出首款商用 MRAM 芯片；近年来，自旋转移矩 MR: Freescale introduced the first commercial MRAM chip in 2006. More recently, spin-transfer-torque MRAM has entered advanced foundry processes as embedded memory.
MRAM 用于工业控制、汽车和航天等需要可靠非易失存储的场合，是替代嵌入式闪存的: MRAM serves industrial control, vehicles, aerospace and other applications needing reliable nonvolatile storage. It is a strong candidate to replace embedded flash.
纳米级半导体颗粒，尺寸决定发光颜色，用于 QLED 显示，2023 年获诺贝尔化: Nanoscale semiconductor particles whose size determines their emission color, used in QLED displays and recognized by the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
把电子关在几纳米大小的半导体颗粒里，它的能级就会像\"盒子中的粒子\"一样变得分: Confining electrons in a semiconductor particle only a few nanometers across gives them discrete energy levels, like a particle in a box. Smaller particles have wider level spacings ([[p:levels|energy levels]]). Changing particle size alone therefore lets the same material emit different colors, from red to blue.
在高温溶液中让半导体晶体成核生长。量子点受蓝光激发后发出纯度很高的颜色，用作显示: Semiconductor crystals are nucleated and grown in a hot solution. Excited by blue light, quantum dots emit highly pure colors. Used as a display’s color-conversion layer, they produce more vivid images.
1981 年，苏联物理学家叶基莫夫在玻璃中发现了量子点；1983 年布鲁斯在溶液: Alexey Ekimov discovered quantum dots in glass in 1981. Louis Brus observed the effect in solution in 1983. Moungi Bawendi developed a method for synthesizing high-quality quantum dots in 1993. They shared the 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
量子点已用于高端电视和显示器，也用于生物荧光标记。: Quantum dots are used in high-end televisions and monitors, as well as fluorescent labels in biology.
把数据编码成 DNA 碱基序列，1 克 DNA 理论上能存约数百 PB，可保存上: Encodes data in DNA base sequences. In theory, a gram of DNA can store hundreds of petabytes and preserve them for more than a thousand years.
DNA 用四种碱基编码遗传信息，本身就是一种极其紧凑、稳定的存储介质（[[p:i: DNA encodes genetic information with four bases and is an exceptionally compact, stable storage medium ([[p:info|information encoding]]). Converting binary data into base sequences gives about 2 bits per base. In cold, dry conditions, the DNA can last thousands of years.
先把数据编码成 A、T、C、G 序列并加上纠错码，再用化学方法合成这些 DNA: Data is encoded as A, T, C and G sequences with error-correcting codes, then chemically synthesized into DNA fragments for storage. A sequencer reads them back, and decoding reconstructs the data. Because each fragment is short, address labels are needed to put them in order.
2012 年，哈佛大学的丘奇（George Church）团队把一本书写进了 D: In 2012, George Church’s Harvard team stored a book in DNA. A 2017 study estimated a storage density of about 215 PB per gram.
它被视为长期冷存档的候选方案；但合成和测序的成本仍然很高、速度很慢，离商用还有很: DNA is a candidate for long-term cold archives, but synthesis and sequencing remain expensive and slow, leaving large barriers to commercial use.
每秒百亿亿次（10¹⁸）浮点运算的超级计算机，2022 年美国 Frontier: Supercomputers capable of 10¹⁸ floating-point operations per second. The US Frontier system first officially reached this level in 2022.
很多科学问题的计算量随分辨率急剧增加，要更精细地模拟气候、核聚变或蛋白质，就需要: Many scientific simulations become dramatically more demanding as resolution increases. More detailed climate, fusion and protein models require faster computers, achieved by connecting tens of thousands of CPUs and GPUs for parallel computation ([[p:division|division of labor and parallelism]]).
E 级超算由上万个计算节点组成，节点之间用高速网络相连；最大的挑战是功耗、散热和: An exascale supercomputer contains more than ten thousand computing nodes linked by a high-speed network. Power consumption, cooling and data movement are its largest challenges; system power reaches roughly 20–30 megawatts.
In May 2022, Frontier at Oak Ridge National Laboratory became the first officially recognized exascale supercomputer, achieving 1.1 × 10¹⁸ floating-point operations per second.
E 级超算被用于气候、材料、大型 AI 模型训练；而最大的 AI 训练集群在算力: Exascale systems support climate research, materials science and large AI training. The largest AI training clusters already exceed traditional supercomputers in computing power.
机器人做实验、AI 决定下一步做什么，让材料和药物发现日夜不停地迭代。: Robots perform experiments while AI chooses what to try next, allowing materials and drug discovery to continue around the clock.
材料和药物研发靠大量\"试错\"，而人做实验慢、会疲劳。让机器人执行实验，让 A: Materials and drug research require extensive trial and error, while human experimenters are slow and become tired. Robots can run experiments, and AI can use the results to select the next set, creating a continuous feedback loop ([[p:feedback|feedback]], [[p:optimization|optimization]]).
机器人负责称量、混合、加热和测量，数据自动上传；算法用贝叶斯优化等方法估计哪些配: Robots weigh, mix, heat and measure, automatically recording the data. Algorithms such as Bayesian optimization estimate which formulations are most promising and direct experiments toward the most informative choices rather than trying every option blindly.
2009 年，英国的\"机器人科学家\"Adam 自主发现了酵母基因的功能；20: In 2009, the UK robot scientist Adam independently discovered functions of yeast genes. In 2020, the University of Liverpool’s mobile robot chemist completed 688 experiments autonomously in 8 days.
它能把材料筛选的速度提高数十倍；但目前适用于流程标准化的实验，结果的可靠性仍需要: This approach can accelerate materials screening by tens of times. It currently suits standardized experimental procedures, and humans must still oversee the reliability of the results.
由几个分子组成、能在外界刺激下转动或移动的纳米结构，获 2016 年诺贝尔化学奖: Nanoscale structures made from a few molecules that rotate or move in response to external stimuli, recognized by the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
生命本身充满了分子机器，比如合成 ATP 的旋转马达和沿着细胞骨架\"行走\"的: Life is full of molecular machines, including rotary motors that produce ATP and motor proteins that walk along the cytoskeleton. Chemists use mechanically interlocked structures, such as linked rings or rings threaded onto axles ([[p:structure|molecular structure]]), to create controlled rotation and movement driven by light, heat or chemical signals.
在轮烷中，一个环形分子套在一根哑铃状的轴上，可以在两个停靠点之间来回穿梭；分子马: In a rotaxane, a ring-shaped molecule encircles a dumbbell-shaped axle and moves between two docking sites. A molecular motor can rotate continuously in one direction under illumination.
1983 年，索瓦日（Jean-Pierre Sauvage）合成了环环相扣的索: Jean-Pierre Sauvage synthesized interlocked catenane rings in 1983. Fraser Stoddart synthesized a rotaxane in 1991, and Ben Feringa built a light-driven molecular motor in 1999. They shared the 2016 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
它开辟了分子尺度的\"机械工程\"，在智能材料、药物释放和分子计算等方向上仍处于: This opened a form of mechanical engineering at molecular scale. Smart materials, controlled drug release and molecular computing remain early research applications.
电阻值能\"记住\"历史的器件，可在存储单元里直接做矩阵乘法，绕开冯·诺依曼瓶颈: A device whose resistance remembers its history. It can perform matrix multiplication where data is stored, bypassing the von Neumann bottleneck.
在冯·诺依曼架构中，数据要在内存和处理器之间来回搬运（[[p:locality|: In von Neumann architectures, data moves repeatedly between memory and processor ([[p:locality|locality]]). A memristor can retain many different resistance values. By Ohm’s law, voltage multiplied by conductance gives current ([[p:ohm|Ohm’s law]]), allowing multiplication directly where a weight is stored.
把忆阻器排成交叉阵列，每个交叉点的电导代表矩阵中的一个权重。在各行加上代表输入的: Memristors form a crossbar array, with conductance at each intersection representing a matrix weight. Voltages applied to rows represent inputs; the current emerging from each column is naturally the sum of the products.
1971 年，蔡少棠（Leon Chua）从理论上预言了忆阻器；2008 年，惠: Leon Chua predicted the memristor theoretically in 1971. In 2008, HP Labs announced a titanium-dioxide thin-film implementation.
存内计算被寄望于大幅降低 AI 推理的能耗；但器件一致性仍是难题。: In-memory computing could greatly reduce the energy used for AI inference, but device-to-device consistency remains difficult.
金属离子和有机分子搭成的多孔晶体，一克的内表面积可达数千平方米，用于吸附气体；2: Porous crystals assembled from metal ions and organic molecules. A gram can have thousands of square meters of internal surface for gas adsorption; the field received the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
金属离子像\"关节\"，有机分子像\"连杆\"，两者自组装成规则的三维框架，内部: Metal ions act as joints and organic molecules as connecting rods, self-assembling into regular three-dimensional frameworks filled with nanoscale pores ([[p:structure|structure determines properties]]). A gram can contain thousands of square meters of internal surface. Pore sizes and chemistry can be designed to selectively adsorb particular gas molecules ([[p:diffusion|diffusion and adsorption]]).
把金属盐和有机配体在溶液中加热，它们就会结晶成多孔框架。用于从烟气或空气中捕集二: Heating metal salts and organic ligands in solution makes them crystallize into porous frameworks. Applications include capturing carbon dioxide from flue gas or air and storing hydrogen.
1999 年，奥马尔·亚吉（Omar Yaghi）报道了稳定的多孔材料 MOF-: Omar Yaghi reported the stable porous material MOF-5 in 1999. Susumu Kitagawa and Richard Robson also made foundational contributions. The three received the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
已有数万种 MOF 被合成出来，少数已用于碳捕集示范和气体储存等商业场景。: Tens of thousands of MOFs have been synthesized. A small number are already used commercially in carbon-capture demonstrations, gas storage and related applications.
表面导电、内部绝缘等性质由电子结构的\"拓扑\"决定，不怕杂质干扰，被寄望用于低: Properties such as conducting surfaces and insulating interiors follow from the topology of electronic structure and can resist impurity effects, offering prospects for low-power electronics and topological qubits.
有些性质不取决于材料的细节，而取决于整体的\"形状\"，就像甜甜圈和咖啡杯都有一: Some properties depend on an overall shape rather than material details, much as a doughnut and a coffee cup both have one hole. In a topological insulator, this global property of electron bands ([[p:band|band structure]]) produces an insulating interior and conducting surface whose current resists impurity scattering.
表面电子的运动方向与自旋锁定在一起；某些拓扑结构中还可能出现马约拉纳零能模，用于: Surface electrons’ direction of motion is locked to their spin. Certain topological structures may also host Majorana zero modes, which could be used to build noise-resistant topological qubits.
2016 年，索利斯、霍尔丹和科斯特利茨因拓扑相变理论获诺贝尔物理学奖；2013: Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz received the 2016 Nobel Prize in Physics for theories of topological phase transitions. Xue Qikun’s team first observed the quantum anomalous Hall effect experimentally in 2013.
它为低功耗电子器件和拓扑量子计算提供了新思路，目前仍以基础研究为主。: This offers new approaches to low-power electronics and topological quantum computing, but remains largely fundamental research.
用光催化剂或光电化学电池模仿植物，直接把阳光、水和二氧化碳变成氢气或燃料。: Uses photocatalysts or photoelectrochemical cells to imitate plants, converting sunlight, water and carbon dioxide directly into hydrogen or fuels.
植物用阳光把水和二氧化碳变成糖和氧气，但能量转化效率只有约 1%（[[p:pho: Plants use sunlight to turn water and carbon dioxide into sugars and oxygen, with energy-conversion efficiency of about 1% ([[p:photosynthesis|photosynthesis]]). Semiconductors can absorb sunlight to create electrons and holes, while catalysts drive water splitting or carbon-dioxide reduction ([[p:catalysis|catalysis]]), potentially storing sunlight directly as fuel.
光催化剂颗粒撒在水中，受光照后在表面产生氢气和氧气；光电化学电池则把光吸收和催化: Photocatalyst particles dispersed in water produce hydrogen and oxygen at their surfaces under illumination. Photoelectrochemical cells allow light absorption and catalysis to be designed separately.
1972 年，日本的藤岛昭和本多健一发现二氧化钛电极在紫外光下能分解水；2021: In 1972, Akira Fujishima and Kenichi Honda found that a titanium-dioxide electrode could split water under ultraviolet light. In 2021, a Japanese team demonstrated a 100 m² photocatalytic water-splitting panel for hydrogen production.
它若能实现低成本、高效率，可以把间歇的太阳能变成可储存的燃料；但目前效率、稳定性: If costs fall and efficiency rises enough, artificial photosynthesis could convert intermittent sunlight into storable fuel. Current efficiency, stability and costs remain inadequate.
用透镜成像、感光材料记录光影；达盖尔银版法于 1839 年公开。: Uses lenses to form images and light-sensitive materials to record them. The daguerreotype process was made public in 1839.
摄影要解决两个问题。第一是成像：透镜把物体上每一点发出的光会聚到对应的一点上，在: Photography must solve two problems. First, image formation: a lens gathers light from each point of an object at a corresponding point, forming an inverted image at the back of a dark box ([[p:optics|optics]]). Second, recording: some chemicals change when exposed to light. Silver-halide crystals absorb photons and release tiny amounts of metallic silver, forming an invisible “latent image” ([[p:photoelectric|light–matter interactions]]). Developer amplifies it into visible black silver grains.
① 曝光：光圈控制进光多少，快门控制曝光时间，两者相乘决定了胶片接收的光量。: ① Exposure: the aperture controls how much light enters, and the shutter controls exposure time. Together they determine how much light reaches the film.
② 显影与定影：显影液把带有潜影的卤化银晶体整颗还原成银，定影液洗掉未曝光的卤化: ② Development and fixing: developer reduces entire silver-halide crystals containing a latent image to silver. Fixer washes away unexposed silver halide, making the image insensitive to further light.
③ 负片与正片：胶片上亮处变黑，得到明暗相反的负片；再把光透过负片照到相纸上，就: ③ Negative and positive: bright areas turn dark on film, producing a negative with reversed tones. Shining light through it onto photographic paper can produce any number of positive prints.
1826 年前后，法国人尼埃普斯（Nicéphore Niépce）拍下了现存最: Around 1826, France’s Nicéphore Niépce made the earliest surviving photograph. In 1839, the French government published Louis Daguerre’s process and offered it freely to the world. Britain’s William Henry Fox Talbot announced his own method that year; his later negative–positive process underpinned film photography for the next century and a half.
普通人第一次能留下亲人和事件的真实影像；新闻摄影改变了人们认识战争和社会的方式，: Ordinary people could preserve realistic images of relatives and events for the first time. Photojournalism changed how people understood war and society, while scientists used photographic plates to record stars and particle tracks.
早期的长曝光意味着运动的人和车不会留下影像，所以老照片里的街道往往空无一人。: Early photographs required long exposures, so moving people and vehicles often left no image. Streets in old photographs therefore often look deserted.
照相机就是\"暗箱 + 透镜 + 感光材料\"。下方是胶片从曝光到出照片的三步：: A camera is a dark box, a lens and a light-sensitive material. Below are the three stages from exposure to a photograph: latent image → development → printing a positive from the negative.
柯达\"你按快门，其余交给我们\"，让摄影进入普通家庭。: Kodak’s “You press the button, we do the rest” brought photography into ordinary homes.
早期摄影需要笨重的玻璃底片和现场冲洗，只有专业人士能做。把感光乳剂涂在柔韧透明的: Early photography required heavy glass plates and on-site processing, making it a professional activity. Coating a flexible, transparent celluloid base with light-sensitive emulsion ([[p:polymer|polymers]]) and rolling it up made cameras smaller and cheaper.
胶卷装在相机里，每拍一张就卷过一格；拍完后把整台相机或胶卷寄回工厂，由工厂负责冲: Film is loaded into the camera and advanced one frame after each shot. Once finished, the whole camera or roll is sent back to the factory for processing, printing and reloading. Photography was split into pressing the shutter, which anyone could do, and industrial processing.
1888 年，美国人伊士曼（George Eastman）推出柯达相机，口号是\: In 1888, American George Eastman launched the Kodak camera with the slogan “You press the button, we do the rest.” The $1 Brownie camera, introduced in 1900, let children take photographs too.
摄影成为普通家庭的日常，家庭相册、旅游照片由此诞生；赛璐珞胶卷也为电影提供了必要: Photography became part of everyday family life, giving rise to family albums and holiday snapshots. Celluloid film also supplied an essential material for cinema.
柯达克罗姆等多层彩色胶片让彩色照片普及。: Multilayer color films such as Kodachrome made color photography widely available.
人眼只有三种感光细胞，分别对红、绿、蓝最敏感，任何颜色都可以由三种基色混合出来（: Human eyes have three types of color-sensitive cone cells, most responsive to red, green and blue. Mixing three primary colors reproduces a wide range of colors ([[p:levels|light and color]]). Recording these three components separately and recombining them in proportion recreates a color image.
彩色胶片上叠了三层乳剂，分别只对蓝、绿、红光敏感。冲洗时，每一层生成对应的补色染: Color film has three emulsion layers sensitive to blue, green and red. Processing forms their complementary dyes: yellow, magenta and cyan. Light passing through the combined layers, or printing them onto paper, reproduces the original colors.
1861 年，麦克斯韦用三张分色照片演示了彩色成像；1907 年卢米埃尔兄弟推出: In 1861, Maxwell demonstrated color imaging with three color-separated photographs. The Lumière brothers introduced Autochrome plates in 1907, and Kodak launched multilayer Kodachrome film in 1935.
20 世纪 60 年代后彩色照片逐渐成为主流；同样的三基色原理也用在彩色电视、显: Color photographs gradually became mainstream after the 1960s. The same three-primary-color principle underpins color television, displays and digital cameras.
用图像传感器代替胶片，照片变成数据；发明它的柯达后来被它颠覆。: Replaces film with an image sensor, turning photographs into data. Kodak invented it but was later disrupted by it.
图像传感器上的每个像素是一个微小的光电二极管，光子打进去会激发出电子（[[p:p: Each pixel on an image sensor is a tiny photodiode. Incoming photons excite electrons ([[p:photoelectric|photoelectric effect]]); stronger light produces more electrons. Reading each pixel’s charge and converting it into a number ([[p:sampling|sampling and quantization]]) turns a photograph into data.
传感器表面覆盖着红绿蓝相间的拜耳滤色阵列，每个像素只记录一种颜色，相机处理器再根: A Bayer filter array covers the sensor with alternating red, green and blue filters. Each pixel records only one color, and the camera processor estimates the full color from neighboring pixels. After white-balance adjustment, noise reduction and [[jpeg|JPEG]] compression, photographs are stored on a memory card for immediate viewing, deletion or copying.
1969 年贝尔实验室的博伊尔和史密斯发明了 CCD 器件，2009 年获诺贝尔: Boyle and Smith at Bell Labs invented the CCD in 1969 and received the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics. In 1975, Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built the first digital camera: just 10,000 pixels, taking 23 seconds to store one photograph.
拍照的边际成本降到几乎为零，人类拍摄的照片数量暴增；胶片产业几乎消失，发明了数码: The marginal cost of taking a photograph fell almost to zero, and the number of photographs soared. The film industry nearly disappeared; Kodak, which had invented the digital camera, filed for bankruptcy protection in 2012.
手机摄像头加上多帧合成和 AI 算法，小镜头也能拍出好照片。: Phone cameras combine multiple frames and AI algorithms to make good photographs with small lenses.
手机镜头和传感器很小，单张照片的进光量和画质天生受限。但计算可以弥补光学：连续拍: Phone lenses and sensors are small, inherently limiting the light and image quality of a single exposure. Computation can compensate: aligning and averaging several consecutive images reduces noise ([[p:probability|statistical averaging]]), while bright and dark regions can be combined in one photograph.
按下快门前后，手机已经连续拍了十几帧，算法对齐、合并、去噪，并做高动态范围合成；: Before and after the shutter press, the phone captures a dozen or so frames. Algorithms align, merge and denoise them, then combine them into a high-dynamic-range image. AI recognizes scenes and automatically adjusts color and sharpness.
2000 年，日本夏普推出第一款内置摄像头的商用手机；2010 年代，谷歌、苹果: Japan’s Sharp launched the first commercial phone with a built-in camera in 2000. In the 2010s, computational photography from Google, Apple, Huawei and others greatly improved phone photography at night.
手机成为世界上最常用的相机；人人都能随时拍摄和发布图片，社交媒体和新闻传播随之改: Phones became the world’s most-used cameras. Anyone can photograph and publish at any time, changing social media and news reporting.
探测物体自身发出的红外辐射，\"看见\"温度分布，用于测温、夜视和检修。: Detects infrared radiation emitted by objects to “see” temperature patterns, for temperature measurement, night vision and inspection.
任何高于绝对零度的物体都在辐射电磁波，温度越高辐射越强，常温物体的辐射集中在人眼: Every object above absolute zero emits electromagnetic radiation, with hotter objects radiating more strongly. At ordinary temperatures, much of this radiation lies in the invisible mid-infrared band ([[p:heat|thermal radiation]], [[p:emwave|electromagnetic waves]]). Measuring infrared intensity at each point produces a temperature map.
红外镜头把辐射聚焦到微测辐射热计阵列上；每个像素吸收红外线后温度微升，电阻随之改: An infrared lens focuses radiation onto a microbolometer array. Each pixel warms slightly as it absorbs infrared, changing its resistance. Reading this change allows temperature to be estimated, without external illumination.
1800 年，天文学家威廉·赫歇尔用温度计发现了可见光谱红端之外的\"看不见的光: In 1800, astronomer William Herschel used thermometers to discover invisible light beyond the red end of the visible spectrum. After uncooled infrared-detector technology was declassified in the 1990s, thermal cameras became compact and affordable.
热像仪用于电力巡检、建筑漏热检查、消防搜救，也是军事 [[night-visio: Thermal cameras are used to inspect power equipment and building heat leaks, locate people in fires and support military [[night-vision|night vision]].
把图像切成网格，每个格子用几个数字记录颜色；分辨率就是格子的多少。: Divides an image into a grid and records each cell’s color with numbers. Resolution describes how many cells it contains.
一幅连续的图像可以切成密密的小方格，每个格子只用一种颜色表示；只要格子足够小，人: A continuous image can be divided into tiny squares, each represented by one color. If the squares are small enough, our eyes cannot distinguish them ([[p:sampling|sampling]]). Expressing each cell’s color numerically turns an image into data a computer can process.
常见的彩色图像里，每个像素由红、绿、蓝三个数值组成，每个值用 8 位表示 0–2: In a typical color image, each pixel contains red, green and blue values, each stored in 8 bits from 0 to 255. Together they represent about 16.77 million colors. Resolution is the total pixel count: a 4K image has roughly 8.3 million pixels.
1957 年，美国国家标准局的基尔希（Russell Kirsch）把儿子的照片: In 1957, Russell Kirsch at the US National Bureau of Standards scanned a photograph of his son into a computer, creating the first digital image at just 176×176 pixels.
像素让图像可以被计算机存储、编辑和传输，修图和数字艺术都建立在这个网格之上。: Pixels allow computers to store, edit and transmit images. Photo editing and digital art rest on this grid.
爱迪生用针在锡箔上刻下声音振动的轨迹，第一次让声音可以被录下并重放。: Edison used a needle to trace sound vibrations in tinfoil, making sound recordable and replayable for the first time.
声音是空气的振动（[[p:wave|波动]]）。让一根针随声波振动，在旋转的介质: Sound is vibration traveling through air ([[p:wave|waves]]). A needle vibrating with sound cuts a varying groove into a moving medium, “freezing” sound into geometry. In reverse, a needle following that groove recreates the original vibration and moves air to produce sound again.
爱迪生的留声机由喇叭收集声音，带动振膜和针，在包着锡箔的圆筒上刻出深浅变化的螺旋: Edison’s phonograph collected sound through a horn, driving a diaphragm and needle to cut a spiral groove of varying depth in a tinfoil-covered cylinder. During playback, the groove vibrated the needle, and the diaphragm and horn amplified the sound. Later records used flat discs and side-to-side grooves.
1857 年，法国人斯科特发明的\"声波记振仪\"能把声音画在纸上，但无法回放。: In 1857, France’s Scott invented the phonautograph, which drew sound on paper but could not play it back. In 1877, Thomas Edison recited “Mary Had a Little Lamb” into his phonograph, recording and replaying a human voice. Emile Berliner invented the flat-disc record in 1887.
音乐第一次可以脱离演奏者被保存、复制和销售，唱片工业诞生；人们可以在家里反复聆听: For the first time, music could be preserved, copied and sold separately from its performers, creating the recording industry. People could repeatedly hear leading performers at home, and popular music spread rapidly worldwide.
麦克风把声波变成电信号，扬声器反过来用电流推动纸盆发声。: Microphones convert sound waves into electrical signals; loudspeakers reverse this, using current to move a cone and produce sound.
声能和电能可以互相转换：线圈在磁场中运动会产生电流（[[p:induction|: Sound energy and electrical energy can be converted into each other. A coil moving in a magnetic field generates current ([[p:induction|electromagnetic induction]]); conversely, a current-carrying coil experiences a force in that field ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]). The same structure can function as a microphone in one direction and a loudspeaker in the other.
动圈麦克风里，声波推动振膜和线圈在磁铁间移动，产生与声音同步变化的电压；扬声器里: In a moving-coil microphone, sound moves a diaphragm and coil within a magnetic field, generating a voltage that follows the sound. In a loudspeaker, varying current moves the coil and cone back and forth, pushing air to produce sound.
1876 年贝尔的电话机中就包含了最早的麦克风和听筒；1925 年，美国通用电气: Bell’s 1876 telephone already contained an early microphone and receiver. In 1925, Rice and Kellogg at General Electric in the United States invented the moving-coil loudspeaker.
它们是电话、广播、有声电影、录音和扩音系统的起点；今天每部手机里都装着好几个微型: These devices underpin telephones, broadcasting, sound films, recording and public-address systems. Modern phones contain several miniature microphones and speakers.
用磁化强弱记录声音，后来发展出磁带、录像带和硬盘。: Records sound as variations in magnetization, later giving rise to audio tape, videotape and hard drives.
铁磁材料被磁化后会保持磁性（[[p:induction|电磁感应]]）。让声音信: Ferromagnetic materials retain magnetization ([[p:induction|electromagnetic induction]]). A sound signal becomes current through a recording head, leaving a changing magnetic pattern on moving tape. During playback, that pattern induces the original electrical signal in the head.
磁带是涂有氧化铁粉末的塑料带，以恒定速度经过录音磁头。录音时同时加入一个高频偏置: Magnetic tape is plastic coated with iron-oxide particles, passing a recording head at a constant speed. Adding a high-frequency bias during recording greatly reduces distortion. The magnetization can be erased and recorded again, making recording inexpensive, flexible and editable by cutting and splicing.
1898 年，丹麦工程师鲍尔森（Valdemar Poulsen）发明钢丝录音机: Danish engineer Valdemar Poulsen invented the wire recorder in 1898. Germany’s AEG and BASF introduced plastic-tape recorders in the 1930s. In 1948, American Ampex recorders made prerecorded radio broadcasts practical.
多轨录音让音乐制作进入录音棚时代；同样的原理后来发展出录像带、计算机磁带和 [[: Multitrack recording brought music production into the studio era. The same principle later produced videotape, computer tape and [[hard-disk-drive|hard drives]].
索尼随身听让音乐可以随身携带，后来 MP3 播放器和手机延续了这一路线。: Sony’s Walkman made music portable, a path later followed by MP3 players and phones.
把音乐装进口袋，需要三样东西都变小：存储介质、播放机构和耳机。小盒式磁带加上低功: Putting music in a pocket requires three things to shrink: storage, playback machinery and headphones. Compact cassettes, low-power electronics and lightweight headphones made high-fidelity music portable ([[p:scale|miniaturization]]).
随身听去掉了录音功能和扬声器，只保留磁带播放机构、放大电路和轻巧的头戴耳机，用几: The Walkman omitted recording and speakers, retaining the tape mechanism, amplifier and lightweight headphones. A few batteries powered it for hours. Later MP3 players replaced tape with flash memory, expanding capacity from dozens of songs to over a thousand.
1979 年，索尼推出第一款随身听 Walkman；2001 年苹果推出 iPo: Sony launched the first Walkman in 1979. Apple introduced the iPod in 2001, promising “1,000 songs in your pocket.”
音乐从客厅走向街头，听音乐成了私人化的体验；随身听销量达数亿台，这一路线最终被智: Music moved from the living room into the street, becoming a private listening experience. Walkman sales reached hundreds of millions, and smartphones ultimately absorbed its role.
每秒采样 44100 次、每次 16 位，把音乐变成数字，复制不失真。: Samples sound 44,100 times per second at 16 bits per sample, turning music into numbers that can be copied without degradation.
采样定理指出，只要每秒采样的次数超过信号最高频率的两倍，就能完整还原原始信号（[: The sampling theorem says a signal can be reconstructed fully if the sampling rate exceeds twice its highest frequency ([[p:sampling|sampling theorem]]). Human hearing reaches roughly 20,000 Hz, making 44,100 samples per second sufficient. Digital signals can also be copied without cumulative degradation.
模数转换器每秒测量声音波形 44100 次，每次用 16 位数字记录高度，相当于: An analog-to-digital converter measures the sound waveform 44,100 times per second and records each amplitude with 16 bits, giving 65,536 levels. These numbers are encoded as tiny pits on a disc. A laser reads them, and a digital-to-analog converter reconstructs continuous sound. Error-correcting codes allow playback despite minor scratches.
1982 年，飞利浦和索尼联合推出的 CD 在日本上市，一张光盘可播放约 74: The CD, jointly developed by Philips and Sony, went on sale in Japan in 1982. One disc held about 74 minutes of audio.
CD 在十年内取代了黑胶唱片和磁带；音乐变成数字后，又为 [[mp3|MP3]]: Within a decade, CDs displaced vinyl records and tapes. Digitized music then paved the way for [[mp3|MP3]], online downloads and streaming.
采样与量化：每隔固定时间测一次波形高度（采样），再把高度取整到最近的台阶（量化）: Sampling and quantization: measure the waveform at regular intervals, then round each amplitude to the nearest available level. Finer levels and more frequent samples give a closer reconstruction.
利用人耳听不到被掩蔽的声音这一特点丢掉冗余信息，文件缩小约十倍。: Discards redundant audio that human hearing cannot detect because of masking, shrinking files by roughly tenfold.
CD 音质每秒要用约 1400 千比特的数据，但其中很多声音人耳根本听不到：一个: CD-quality audio uses about 1,400 kilobits per second, yet much of it is inaudible. A loud sound masks quieter sounds at nearby frequencies, and hearing is less sensitive at very high or low frequencies. Using these psychoacoustic effects to retain perceptible information greatly reduces data ([[p:info|information and compression]]).
编码器把声音切成很短的片段，分解到几百个频段，计算每个频段此刻的\"掩蔽阈值\": The encoder splits sound into brief segments and hundreds of frequency bands, calculating a masking threshold for each. Components below it are discarded, and the rest receive precision according to hearing sensitivity. A 128-kilobit-per-second MP3 is roughly one-eleventh the size of CD audio, with differences many listeners cannot hear.
德国弗劳恩霍夫研究所的勃兰登堡（Karlheinz Brandenburg）等人: Karlheinz Brandenburg and colleagues at Germany’s Fraunhofer Institute led development. The algorithm was published as MPEG-1 Layer III audio in 1993; Napster enabled large-scale online MP3 sharing in 1999.
一首歌从几十兆字节变成几兆字节，可以在拨号网络上传送；唱片业经历了盗版冲击，之后: A song shrank from tens of megabytes to just a few, making dial-up transfer practical. The recording industry faced widespread piracy, followed by iTunes downloads and [[streaming-media|streaming]].
每秒连续放映十几到二十几张照片，利用视觉暂留形成动态画面。: Projects roughly a dozen to a few dozen photographs per second, creating moving images through visual perception.
快速连续呈现一系列略有差别的静止画面，大脑会把它们感知为连续的运动（[[p:sa: When slightly different still images appear in rapid succession, the brain perceives continuous motion ([[p:sampling|sampling in time]]). Motion becomes apparent at roughly a dozen frames per second; 24 frames per second already looks fairly smooth.
摄影机以固定速度拍摄连续的画面，每拍一格，胶片就停顿一下再前进；放映机以同样的节: A movie camera records successive frames at a fixed rate, pausing the film for each exposure before advancing it. A projector uses the same rhythm to project each frame. A shutter blocks light during frame changes, hiding the film’s movement from the audience.
1878 年，迈布里奇用一排相机拍下奔马的连续照片；1891 年前后，爱迪生公司: In 1878, Muybridge used a row of cameras to photograph a running horse in sequence. Around 1891, Dickson at Edison’s company built the Kinetoscope. On December 28, 1895, the Lumière brothers screened films for paying customers in a Paris café, an event commonly treated as cinema’s birth.
电影成为 20 世纪最有影响力的大众艺术和娱乐形式，也是宣传工具；好莱坞等电影工: Cinema became one of the twentieth century’s most influential mass art and entertainment forms, as well as a propaganda medium. Industries such as Hollywood emerged, and television and online video inherited cinema’s visual language.
常说的\"视觉暂留\"并不是运动感的真正原因，现代研究认为主要是大脑对运动的主动: The commonly cited “persistence of vision” is not the main cause of perceived motion. Modern research emphasizes the brain’s active inference of movement.
把声音以光学轨迹印在胶片边缘，与画面同步播放。: Prints sound as an optical track along the film’s edge, keeping it synchronized with the picture.
要让声音和画面严格同步，最可靠的办法是把它们记录在同一条胶片上。把声音信号变成胶: The most reliable way to synchronize sound and pictures is to record both on the same film. An optical soundtrack of varying width or density along its edge represents the audio signal through changes in transmitted light ([[p:sampling|synchronized recording]]).
放映时，一束光穿过运动中的声迹，照到光电管上，产生随声迹变化的电流，经放大后驱动: During projection, a light beam passes through the moving soundtrack onto a photocell, producing a varying current that is amplified to drive a speaker. The soundtrack and pictures are printed on the same strip of film.
1923 年，德福雷斯特展示了把声音印在胶片上的有声片系统；1927 年《爵士歌: In 1923, De Forest demonstrated a sound-on-film system. The Jazz Singer was a major success in 1927, although it used a record synchronized with the film. Optical soundtracks became the industry standard a few years later.
短短几年内无声片被淘汰；电影的帧率也因此固定为每秒 24 格。: Silent films were displaced within a few years. Sound also helped standardize cinema at 24 frames per second.
把画面逐行扫描成电信号、通过无线电发送、在接收端重新扫描还原。: Scans an image line by line into an electrical signal, transmits it by radio and scans it again at the receiver to reconstruct it.
画面是二维的，而无线电信号一次只能传一个数值。电视的解决办法是扫描：把画面分成几: An image has two dimensions, but a radio signal carries one value at a time. Television solves this through scanning: divide the image into hundreds of lines and read brightness point by point, left to right and top to bottom, producing a time-varying signal ([[p:sampling|sampling and scanning]]). The receiver redraws bright points in the same sequence and rhythm. Scanning dozens of complete images per second creates continuous moving pictures.
① 摄像：早期的摄像管把画面的光转换成电荷图像，再用电子束逐行扫描读出电信号。: ① Capture: early camera tubes converted light into a charge image, which an electron beam scanned line by line to produce an electrical signal.
② 发送：图像信号和同步信号调制到高频载波上，通过电视塔以 [[p:emwave: ② Transmission: picture and synchronization signals modulate a high-frequency carrier, broadcast from a television tower as [[p:emwave|electromagnetic waves]].
③ 显示：显像管里的电子束在磁场控制下逐行扫过荧光屏，信号强时电子多，那一点就亮: ③ Display: magnetic fields steer an electron beam line by line across a phosphor screen. A stronger signal supplies more electrons, making that point brighter. Synchronization signals keep transmitter and receiver scanning together.
1884 年，德国人尼普科夫提出用带孔的旋转圆盘扫描图像。1926 年 1 月，: In 1884, Germany’s Nipkow proposed scanning images with a rotating perforated disc. Britain’s John Logie Baird publicly demonstrated mechanical television in January 1926. In 1927, American Philo Farnsworth transmitted an image electronically. The BBC began regular television broadcasts in 1936.
电视让数以亿计的人同时看到同一场画面，1969 年阿波罗登月吸引了全球约 6 亿: Television let hundreds of millions watch the same event simultaneously. Apollo’s 1969 Moon landing drew roughly 600 million viewers worldwide. It reshaped elections, news, sport and advertising, becoming a center of domestic life in the later twentieth century.
为了在有限的带宽里减少闪烁，早期电视采用\"隔行扫描\"：先扫奇数行，再扫偶数行: To reduce flicker within limited bandwidth, early television used interlaced scanning: odd-numbered lines first, then even-numbered lines, transmitting half an image at a time.
电视的扫描与还原：摄像端把画面逐行读成一条电信号，接收端的电子束按同样的顺序和节: Television scanning and reconstruction: the camera reads an image line by line into an electrical signal, and the receiver’s electron beam redraws the bright points in the same order and rhythm.
用红绿蓝三基色合成所有颜色，并兼容黑白电视。: Combines red, green and blue to reproduce color while remaining compatible with black-and-white television.
彩色电视同样利用三基色：任何颜色都能由红、绿、蓝三种光按不同比例混合出来（[[p: Color television uses three primary colors, mixing red, green and blue light in different proportions ([[p:levels|light and color]]). The crucial challenge was compatibility: existing black-and-white sets had to remain able to display color broadcasts.
信号被拆成亮度和色度两部分：黑白电视只接收亮度信号；彩色电视再解出色度信号，控制: The signal is separated into luminance and chrominance. Black-and-white televisions use luminance alone. Color sets also decode chrominance to control three electron guns striking red, green and blue phosphors. Chrominance is fitted into gaps in the luminance spectrum, avoiding wider channels.
1953 年，美国批准了兼容黑白电视的 NTSC 彩色电视标准；1967 年，联: The United States approved the backward-compatible NTSC color standard in 1953. West Germany’s PAL and France’s SECAM broadcasts began in 1967.
20 世纪 70 年代起彩电在发达国家普及，中国在 80 年代迎来了彩电热；三种: Color television spread across developed countries from the 1970s, with a boom in China during the 1980s. The three incompatible systems required conversions when exchanging programs.
把电视信号录在磁带上，让人可以在家随时观看节目。: Records television signals on magnetic tape so people can watch programs at home whenever they choose.
电视信号的频率比声音高几百倍，固定磁头和普通磁带速度跟不上。让磁头装在高速旋转的: Television signals have frequencies hundreds of times higher than audio. Fixed heads and ordinary tape speeds cannot keep up. Mounting heads on a rapidly rotating drum lets them sweep diagonally across slowly moving tape at a sufficiently high relative speed ([[p:induction|electromagnetic induction]]).
螺旋扫描录像机的磁带斜着绕在旋转磁鼓上，每转一圈，磁头就在磁带上划出一条斜向的磁: In a helical-scan recorder, tape wraps diagonally around a rotating drum. Each turn traces a diagonal magnetic track recording one field of video. Audio and control signals run along the tape’s edges.
