地球的温度取决于吸收和散失的能量（[[p:heat|能量平衡]]）。如果向平流层: Earth’s temperature depends on absorbed and outgoing energy ([[p:heat|energy balance]]). Particles in the stratosphere reflecting roughly 1% of sunlight could offset substantial warming; large volcanic eruptions have temporarily cooled the planet.
太阳辐射管理设想用高空飞机在平流层释放硫酸盐气溶胶，或者向海洋上空喷洒盐雾让云变: Solar-radiation-management proposals include releasing sulfate aerosols from high-altitude aircraft or spraying sea salt to brighten marine clouds. Large-scale carbon removal is another approach, usually classified as [[carbon-dioxide-removal|carbon dioxide removal]].
1991 年菲律宾皮纳图博火山喷发后，全球平均气温在一两年内下降了约 0.5 °: After Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines in 1991, global temperature fell roughly 0.5°C for a year or two. Nobel laureate Paul Crutzen called for serious research into this option in 2006.
它可能是\"紧急刹车\"，但无法解决海洋酸化，还可能改变降雨模式；一旦停止，温度: It might act as an emergency brake, but would not solve ocean acidification and could change rainfall. Abrupt cessation could cause rapid warming. Deciding who controls a global temperature intervention poses a major governance problem.
微生物在无氧条件下分解粪便和有机垃圾产生甲烷，可用于发电和炊事。: Microbes break down manure and organic waste without oxygen, producing methane for cooking and electricity.
在没有氧气的环境里，一系列微生物接力，把有机物一步步分解，最后由产甲烷菌产生甲烷: Without oxygen, successive microbial groups break down organic matter, ending with methane-producing organisms that release methane and carbon dioxide ([[p:bond|chemical energy]]). Capturing this gas as fuel avoids letting manure and food waste release it directly.
粪便、秸秆或厨余送入密封的消化罐，在 35 °C 左右发酵几周，产出约含六成甲烷: Manure, straw or food waste enters sealed digesters and ferments for weeks around 35°C. The resulting biogas contains roughly 60% methane and can fuel cooking or power generation, or be upgraded for gas networks. Residual solids and liquids can serve as fertilizer.
20 世纪 70 年代起，中国和印度在农村推广了数以千万计的户用沼气池；德国在本: From the 1970s, China and India promoted tens of millions of household digesters. Renewable-energy support helped Germany build over ten thousand biogas power plants in the early twenty-first century.
沼气同时解决了能源、卫生和肥料问题；它还是减少农业和垃圾甲烷排放的有效手段，但沼: Biogas combines energy, sanitation and fertilizer benefits and can reduce agricultural and waste methane emissions. Poorly managed digesters can leak or fall out of use.
把垃圾分层压实、每天覆土，底部铺防渗层并收集渗滤液和填埋气，避免污染地下水。: Compacts waste in layers with daily soil cover, a sealed base and collection of leachate and landfill gas to protect groundwater.
垃圾简单堆放会引来蚊蝇鼠虫，渗出的污水还会渗入地下水；垃圾在缺氧条件下分解产生甲: Open dumps attract pests and release polluted liquid into groundwater. Oxygen-poor decomposition also generates methane ([[p:bond|chemical energy]]). Isolating waste from its surroundings ([[p:diffusion|blocking diffusion]]) and collecting liquids and gases substantially reduces harm.
填埋场底部铺设压实黏土和高密度聚乙烯防渗膜，垃圾分层摊铺压实，每天覆盖泥土。底部: The base combines compacted clay and a high-density polyethylene liner. Waste is spread and compacted in layers with daily soil cover. Bottom pipes collect leachate for treatment; wells collect gas for power generation or flaring. Closed sites receive soil and vegetation and require long-term monitoring.
20 世纪 30–40 年代，美国和英国开始推广每日覆土的卫生填埋方法，此后防渗: The United States and United Kingdom promoted sanitary landfilling with daily cover in the 1930s–1940s. Lining and gas-collection requirements developed later.
城市告别了露天垃圾场；但填埋场仍是人为甲烷的主要来源之一，越来越多的国家限制可回: Cities moved beyond open dumps, but landfills remain a major human-caused methane source. More countries restrict recyclable and combustible waste from landfills.
万维网建立在三项简单的发明上：**URL**（统一资源定位符），说明用什么协议、: The World Wide Web rests on three simple inventions: **URL** (Uniform Resource Locator) specifies the protocol, server and file; **HTML** describes headings, paragraphs, images and links with markup; **HTTP** defines browser requests and server responses (see [[http-html]]). When you click a link, the [[web-browser|browser]] uses its URL to find the server, retrieve HTML and render the page.
合成氨化肥让粮食产量成倍增长，据估计全球约一半人口的食物依赖它（见 [[chem: Synthetic-ammonia fertilizers multiplied crop yields; roughly half the world’s population is estimated to depend on them for food (see [[chemical-fertilizer]]). The history also has a darker side: Germany used the process for explosives in World War I, and Haber himself directed chemical warfare. Ammonia production consumes about 2% of global energy. Producing green ammonia with hydrogen from [[electrolysis|water electrolysis]] is one route to reducing emissions.
一人可同时纺多根纱的手摇纺纱机，拉开了纺织机械化的序幕。: A hand-powered spinning machine let one person spin several threads at once, beginning the mechanization of textiles.
T 型车价格从 1908 年的 850 美元降到 1920 年代中期的 300: The Model T’s price fell from $850 in 1908 to below $300 by the mid-1920s. Around 15 million were produced, bringing cars to ordinary households (see [[model-t]]). Assembly lines spread across almost every industry, enabling [[mass-production|mass production]]. The cost was repetitive, monotonous work—the subject of Chaplin’s Modern Times (1936).
2002 年美国学者格里夫斯（Michael Grieves）提出这一概念，20: American researcher Michael Grieves proposed the concept in 2002. NASA’s John Vickers coined the name “digital twin” around 2010.
六轴工业机器人：前三个关节决定\"手\"到达的位置，后三个关节决定工具的朝向；每: A six-axis industrial robot: the first three joints position the “hand”; the last three orient the tool. Each joint has its own feedback-control loop.
协作机器人降低了自动化门槛，让中小企业也能使用机器人，人和机器分工协作，而不是简: Collaborative robots lower the barrier to automation for small and medium-sized businesses, allowing people and machines to share tasks rather than simply replacing people.
精简指令集（RISC）使用数量较少、长度固定、格式规整的指令，内存访问只通过专门: Reduced Instruction Set Computer (RISC) uses fewer, fixed-length, and well-formatted instructions, with memory access completed only through dedicated read/write instructions. This allows each instruction to be completed in approximately the same time, which is suitable for [[pipeline|instruction pipelining]]. Complex Instruction Set Computer (CISC), such as x86, allows a single instruction to do many things, resulting in more compact code, but hardware is harder to parallelize.
MIMO（多输入多输出）在收发两端都用多根天线。**空间复用**让多路数据流同时: MIMO (multiple-input, multiple-output) uses several antennas at both transmitter and receiver. **Spatial multiplexing** sends parallel data streams along different spatial paths, multiplying data rates. **Beamforming** directs the signal toward a user like a flashlight, improving strength and reducing interference. **Multi-user MIMO** lets a base station direct separate beams to several users at once.
**量化**把每个参数从 16 位压到 8 位、4 位甚至更低，体积和显存需求成: **Quantization** reduces each parameter from 16 bits to 8, 4 or fewer, cutting model size and memory needs severalfold, often with little accuracy loss. **Distillation** trains a small student to imitate a larger teacher’s output probabilities or reasoning, conveying more than correct answers alone. **Pruning** removes less important connections or structures.
铁矿石、焦炭和石灰石从炉顶分层装入，热风从炉底鼓入。焦炭燃烧产生上千度高温和一氧: Iron ore, coke and limestone enter in layers from the furnace top, while hot air enters below. Burning coke produces temperatures above 1,000°C and carbon monoxide. The descending charge is reduced and melted, while limestone binds impurities into floating slag. Molten pig iron containing about 4% carbon leaves the bottom for further refining into steel. Large furnaces produce over 10,000 tons daily and can run continuously for a decade or more.
用无害或减弱的\"假病原体\"预先训练免疫系统，真病原体来时就能迅速消灭它。: Trains immune memory using harmless components or weakened stand-ins for a pathogen, helping the body respond quickly to the real infection.
免疫系统靠\"认形状\"识别入侵者：抗体和免疫细胞能与病原体表面特定的分子（抗原: The immune system recognizes molecular shapes. Antibodies and immune cells bind specific pathogen molecules called antigens ([[p:recognition|molecular recognition]]). A first encounter can require a week or two to build a strong response. Afterwards, **memory cells** remain and can mount a much faster response. Vaccination rehearses this recognition so memory is ready in advance ([[p:germ|germ theory]]).
疫苗有几类：**减毒活疫苗**（麻疹、口服脊灰）用削弱了的活病原体；**灭活疫苗: **Live attenuated vaccines**, such as measles and oral polio vaccines, use weakened pathogens. **Inactivated vaccines** use killed pathogens. **Subunit vaccines**, including hepatitis B and HPV vaccines, use selected proteins. **Toxoids** target bacterial toxins, as in tetanus vaccination. **mRNA vaccines** supply cells with antigen-making instructions (see [[mrna-vaccine]]). When enough people are immune, transmission becomes harder and even unvaccinated people gain indirect protection: **herd immunity**. More contagious diseases require higher coverage; measles requires roughly 95%.
伦琴发现能穿透人体的射线，骨骼会挡住它留下影子，医生第一次\"看进\"活人体内。: Röntgen discovered rays that penetrate the body. Bones absorb more of them and cast shadows, letting doctors see inside living people.
X 射线是波长极短、能量很高的电磁波（[[p:emwave|电磁波]]），能穿透: X-rays are short-wavelength, high-energy electromagnetic waves ([[p:emwave|electromagnetic waves]]) that pass through soft tissue. Calcium-rich bone absorbs more strongly. The resulting detector image shows bones as white, lungs as dark and soft tissues between them.
X 光管里，电子在几万到十几万伏的高压下加速，猛撞钨靶，突然减速时放出 X 射线: Inside an X-ray tube, electrons accelerate through tens to over a hundred thousand volts and strike a tungsten target. Sudden deceleration emits X-rays, which pass through the body to a detector, now often a digital flat panel. As ionizing radiation, X-rays can damage DNA, so exposure is minimized. A chest radiograph typically involves about 0.02–0.1 millisieverts, comparable to no more than roughly ten days of natural background exposure.
弗莱明发现青霉菌能杀菌，弗洛里和钱恩在 1940 年代将青霉素做成药，细菌感染从: Fleming discovered penicillin-producing mold; Florey and Chain developed penicillin into a medicine in the 1940s, transforming treatment of bacterial infections.
抗生素能杀死细菌却不伤害人体，诀窍在于专打细菌有、人类没有的东西（[[p:rec: Antibiotics can act selectively by targeting structures bacteria have that human cells lack ([[p:recognition|molecular recognition]]). Penicillin prevents bacterial cell-wall synthesis. Gaps form as bacteria grow, and internal pressure can rupture them; human cells have no such wall. Other antibiotics target bacterial ribosomes or DNA-replication enzymes ([[p:germ|germ theory]]).
许多抗生素来自微生物自己——霉菌和土壤里的放线菌用它们与细菌争夺地盘。工业上用大: Many antibiotics come from microbes themselves: molds and soil actinomycetes use them in competition. Industry cultures these organisms in large fermenters and purifies the products (see [[fermentation-bioreactor]]), or chemically modifies natural molecules to make semisynthetic antibiotics. Different agents target different bacteria, so clinicians choose according to the infection and organism. Antibiotics do not treat viruses and generally are not used for uncomplicated colds or influenza.
从找靶点、筛化合物到三期临床，新药平均要十年以上、花费十亿美元级别。: From target discovery and compound screening through three clinical phases, developing a new drug commonly takes over a decade and costs on the order of a billion dollars.
大多数药物的作用方式，是一个小分子或抗体与体内某个特定蛋白（靶点）结合，开启或关: Many drugs work by binding a specific protein target and altering its activity ([[p:recognition|molecular recognition]]). Development identifies a disease-related target and a molecule that binds it selectively. Whether a candidate is safe and effective must then be assessed through statistically rigorous human trials ([[p:probability|probability and statistical inference]]).
典型流程像一个漏斗：**靶点发现**（基因和疾病研究）→ **苗头化合物筛选**: The process resembles a funnel: **target discovery** through gene and disease research → **hit screening**, using robots to test tens of thousands of molecules daily or virtual screening → **lead optimization** to improve activity, toxicity and absorption → **preclinical studies** in cells and animals → **three phases of clinical trials** (see [[clinical-trial]]) → regulatory approval → postmarketing monitoring. Protein structures and AI increasingly assist design (see [[protein-structure]], [[ai-for-science]]). Therapeutics now include antibodies, nucleic acids, cells and gene therapies as well as small molecules.
把病毒蛋白的\"图纸\"（mRNA）送入细胞，让身体自己生产抗原；新冠疫苗中首次: Delivers mRNA instructions for a viral protein so cells produce an antigen. COVID-19 vaccines brought the first large-scale use.
细胞按照\"DNA → mRNA → 蛋白质\"的流程制造蛋白质（[[p:dog: Cells make proteins through the sequence DNA → mRNA → protein ([[p:dogma|central dogma]]). An mRNA vaccine supplies instructions for a viral protein rather than the virus itself. Cells temporarily produce the protein, allowing the immune system to learn its identity ([[p:recognition|molecular recognition]]).
mRNA 非常脆弱，进入血液很快就被分解，还会引发强烈炎症。两项关键技术解决了这: mRNA is fragile, readily degraded and can provoke strong inflammation. Two technologies address this: modified nucleosides reduce unwanted immune activation, and lipid nanoparticles protect mRNA and help it enter cells (see [[lipid-nanoparticle]]). The instructions are read in the cytoplasm and break down within days; they do not enter the nucleus or alter human DNA. A major advantage is development speed: a candidate can be designed within days of obtaining the viral sequence, using a broadly shared production process.
沃森和克里克（基于富兰克林的 X 射线照片）提出 DNA 是双螺旋，碱基配对解释: Watson and Crick proposed DNA’s double helix, drawing on Franklin’s X-ray evidence. Complementary base pairing explained how genetic information could be copied.
遗传信息必须能被精确复制。DNA 由两条链像拧麻花一样缠绕而成，链上的碱基两两配: Genetic information must be copied accurately. DNA’s two intertwined strands pair bases specifically: A with T, and G with C ([[p:structure|structure determines properties]]). Each strand therefore specifies the other. Separating them and building complementary partners produces two matching DNA molecules ([[p:dogma|central dogma]]).
每条链的\"骨架\"由糖和磷酸交替连接，碱基朝内，像梯子的横档；A 与 T 之间: Each strand has an alternating sugar–phosphate backbone, with bases pointing inward like ladder rungs. A–T pairs have two hydrogen bonds; G–C pairs have three, balancing stability with separability. Base order encodes information like a long text written with four letters. The human genome contains about 3.1 billion base pairs; cellular DNA extends roughly two meters yet packs into a nucleus only a few micrometers across.
把一种生物的基因剪下来接到另一种生物的 DNA 里，让细菌替人生产胰岛素等蛋白质: Transfers a gene from one organism into another’s DNA, enabling bacteria to make human proteins such as insulin.
遗传密码在所有生物中通用（见 [[genetic-code]]），所以把人的一段: The genetic code is shared across life (see [[genetic-code]]), so bacteria can read an introduced human gene and produce its protein ([[p:dogma|central dogma]]). Cutting and joining DNA lets microbes manufacture medicines.
用限制酶（见 [[restriction-enzyme]]）把目标基因和细菌的环: Restriction enzymes (see [[restriction-enzyme]]) cut a target gene and a small circular bacterial DNA molecule called a plasmid. Ligase joins them, and the recombinant plasmid enters bacteria. An antibiotic-resistance marker helps select cells carrying the plasmid. Bacteria dividing every twenty or thirty minutes rapidly multiply into hundreds of millions of production cells, making protein in fermenters (see [[fermentation-bioreactor]]). More complex proteins may require yeast or mammalian cells.
通过反复加热冷却让 DNA 指数级复制，几小时就能把一个分子扩增到数十亿份。: Repeated heating and cooling amplifies DNA exponentially, potentially producing billions of copies from one molecule within hours.
DNA 复制酶能以一条单链为模板合成互补链（[[p:dogma|中心法则]]）。: DNA polymerase uses one strand as a template to build its complement ([[p:dogma|central dogma]]). PCR repeats this process in a tube. Ideally, each cycle doubles the target, so 30 cycles produce 2³⁰ copies, roughly a billionfold amplification ([[p:exponential|exponential growth]]).
每轮循环分三步，靠温度控制：**变性**（约 95°C）让双链解开；**退火**: Each cycle has three temperature-controlled stages: **denaturation** around 95°C separates strands; **annealing** around 55–65°C lets short synthetic primers bind the target’s ends; **extension** around 72°C lets heat-resistant polymerase build new strands. Cycles take minutes, with an automated instrument completing the process in one or two hours. Taq polymerase, from heat-loving bacteria associated with Yellowstone hot springs, withstands repeated heating. **Quantitative real-time PCR** measures fluorescence during amplification to estimate quantity. Reverse-transcribing RNA into DNA first allows detection of RNA viruses such as SARS-CoV-2.
读出 DNA 上 A、T、C、G 的排列顺序；每个人类基因组的测序成本 20 年: Reads the order of A, T, C and G in DNA. Human-genome sequencing costs fell by over 100,000-fold in roughly twenty years.
测序就是逐个读出 DNA 上 A、T、C、G 的排列顺序。桑格法的巧妙之处是：让: Sequencing determines DNA’s base order. In Sanger sequencing, polymerase copies a template while occasional chain-terminating bases stop extension. This produces fragments ending at different positions. Sorting them by length and reading each final base reveals the sequence ([[p:dogma|central dogma]]).
早期用放射性标记和凝胶电泳读序列（见 [[gel-electrophoresis: Early sequencing used radioactive labels and gel electrophoresis (see [[gel-electrophoresis]]) to read a few hundred bases at a time. Four fluorescent terminators later enabled automated capillary-electrophoresis and laser reading. **High-throughput sequencing** (see [[ngs]]) reads hundreds of millions of fragments in parallel, then computationally assembles them (see [[bioinformatics]]). A human genome cost roughly $100 million around 2001 but only hundreds of dollars around 2022, declining faster than Moore’s law ([[p:scale|economies of scale and learning curves]]).
用一段向导 RNA 带着 Cas9\"剪刀\"精确找到并剪开目标 DNA，基因编: Guide RNA directs the Cas9 molecular scissors to a matching DNA sequence, making gene editing easier and cheaper.
细菌有一套\"免疫记忆\"：把入侵病毒的 DNA 片段存进自己的基因组，再转录成: Bacteria have a form of immune memory: stored viral DNA fragments are transcribed into short RNAs that guide Cas9 to matching invaders for cleavage ([[p:recognition|molecular recognition]]). Changing the guide RNA lets researchers retarget this cutting system to a selected DNA sequence ([[p:dogma|central dogma]]).
向导 RNA 约 20 个碱基，与目标 DNA 互补配对，Cas9 在此切开 D: A guide segment of about 20 bases pairs with complementary target DNA, where Cas9 cuts both strands. Repair by direct rejoining can insert or delete bases and disrupt a gene. With a repair template, the cell may copy a desired change. Earlier methods required a new targeting protein; CRISPR often needs only a new RNA, making it cheaper, faster and broadly adaptable. Challenges include off-target cuts and safe delivery to the intended cells.
机械记录每笔交易并锁住钱箱，减少店员舞弊。: Mechanically records each transaction and locks the cash drawer, reducing employee fraud.
店员舞弊难以杜绝，是因为钱进了钱箱却没留下记录。让\"收钱\"和\"记账\"成为: When money enters a drawer without a record, misconduct is hard to detect. Making payment collection and recording inseparable lets the accounts provide a cross-check ([[p:feedback|feedback and reconciliation]]).
店员按下金额键，机器在顶部亮出数字让顾客看见，同时在纸卷上留下记录、计数器累加，: Pressing an amount key displays it to the customer, prints a paper record and adds it to a counter. The drawer rings when opened. At closing, the owner can compare cash against the paper roll.
1879 年，美国俄亥俄州酒馆老板詹姆斯·里蒂（James Ritty）发明并申: Ohio saloon owner James Ritty patented the machine in 1879 as an “incorruptible cashier.” John H. Patterson bought the patent and founded NCR, spreading cash registers worldwide.
零售业有了逐笔记录，后来的条形码扫描、POS 终端和库存系统都是从这台机器发展出: Retail gained transaction-by-transaction records. Barcode scanning, POS terminals and inventory systems developed from this foundation.
通过电报线实时打印股价的纸带机器，让远方投资者也能跟上市场。: A machine prints live stock prices received by telegraph, letting distant investors follow the market.
价格本身就是信息，谁先知道谁就占优。把价格编码成电报信号，就能以接近光速传到远方: Prices are information, and earlier access provides an advantage. Encoding prices as telegraph signals sends them rapidly over long distances ([[p:info|information and coding]]), extending trading beyond the exchange floor.
交易所的操作员把成交的股票代码和价格敲进发报机，信号沿电报线传到各地经纪行，接收: Exchange operators enter stock symbols and prices into a transmitter. Telegraph lines carry signals to brokers, where electrical pulses rotate type wheels that print hundreds of characters per minute on narrow paper tape.
1867 年，美国电报工程师卡拉汉（Edward Calahan）发明股票报价机: American telegraph engineer Edward Calahan invented the stock ticker in 1867. The young Thomas Edison improved it and used proceeds from selling the invention to establish a laboratory.
全美投资者几乎能同时看到行情，市场连成一体。纽约用纸带庆祝的\"纸带游行\"也由: Investors across the United States could see prices almost simultaneously, linking markets. New York’s ticker-tape parades took their name from the paper strips. Tickers preceded modern real-time quotation systems.
用粗细不同的黑白条表示数字，扫描即可识别商品；1974 年首次在超市使用。: Black and white bars of varying widths encode numbers for scanning products. The first supermarket use was in 1974.
把数字编码成宽窄不同的黑白条纹，光照上去时黑条吸光、白条反光，扫描器读出的是一串: Barcodes represent numbers through narrow and wide dark and light stripes. Dark bars absorb light and light spaces reflect it, producing alternating pulses that scanners decode ([[p:info|information and coding]]). Shared industry rules let a product be recognized in different stores ([[p:standard|standards]]).
最常见的 UPC/EAN 码用 12 或 13 位数字表示国家或厂商和具体商品，: Common UPC/EAN codes use 12 or 13 digits for registration/manufacturer and product identifiers, with a final check digit to detect errors. A laser or camera reads the code, and checkout software looks up the name and price in a database. The barcode stores an identifier, not the price itself.
1949 年伍德兰（Norman Woodland）和西尔弗（Bernard S: Norman Woodland and Bernard Silver applied for an early barcode patent in 1949, inspired by stretching Morse-code marks in sand. US grocers adopted George Laurer’s IBM UPC design in 1973. In June 1974, an Ohio supermarket scanned the first product: a pack of chewing gum.
结账速度大大加快，商店第一次精确知道每件商品卖了多少，库存管理、供应链和 [[l: Checkout accelerated and retailers could track sales precisely, supporting inventory management, supply chains and [[logistics-automation|logistics automation]].
EAN-13 条码的结构：起始符和终止符告诉扫描器从哪里开始；中间的条纹组合表示: EAN-13 structure: start and end markers guide the scanner; bar patterns encode digits, and a final check digit helps detect reading errors.
日本电装发明的二维矩阵码，容量大、可纠错，是扫码支付的基础。: Denso’s two-dimensional matrix code holds more data and corrects errors, becoming a foundation for scan-to-pay systems.
一维条码只能横向编码，容量只有十几个字符；改成二维的黑白方块矩阵，信息量增加上百: A one-dimensional barcode carries only roughly a dozen characters along one axis. A two-dimensional grid of black and white squares increases capacity by over a hundredfold. Redundant error-correction data ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]) allows recovery despite partial damage.
三个角上的\"回\"字形定位图案让摄像头从任何角度都能找到二维码并校正方向，其余: Three nested-square finder patterns let a camera locate and orient the code from different angles. Other squares encode data and error correction. At the highest correction level, substantial damage—roughly 30% in the simplified description—can still permit recovery.
1994 年，日本电装公司（后来的 Denso Wave）的原昌宏为追踪汽车零件: Masahiro Hara at Japan’s Denso, later Denso Wave, invented QR codes in 1994 to track car parts. The company published the specification and did not enforce its relevant patent rights.
智能手机普及后，二维码成为连接线下与线上的通用入口，从扫码支付、健康码到菜单和登: Smartphones made QR codes a common bridge between physical and digital services: payments, health codes, menus and boarding passes can be accessed from a printed sheet.
投币即出货的无人售卖机器，从明信片、饮料到车票，后来接入了扫码支付。: An unattended machine dispenses goods after payment, from postcards and drinks to tickets, later adding QR payments.
把\"验钱\"和\"出货\"变成一个自动的条件判断：只有检测到足够的钱，机械锁才: Payment validation and dispensing become an automatic condition: only sufficient payment releases the mechanical lock holding a product ([[p:feedback|feedback control]]).
早期机器靠硬币的重量和尺寸推动杠杆；现代售货机用电磁传感器测量硬币的材质和直径、: Early machines used coin weight and dimensions to move levers. Modern machines identify coins electromagnetically and scan banknotes optically, then dispense goods with motors. Connected machines can accept QR payments and report low stock remotely.
公元 1 世纪，亚历山大的希罗就描述过投币出圣水的装置；1883 年英国人埃弗里: Hero of Alexandria described a coin-operated holy-water dispenser in the first century AD. Britain’s Percival Everitt invented a postcard vending machine in 1883, beginning commercial vending.
商品可以 24 小时无人售卖；日本是售货机密度最高的国家之一，街头随处可见饮料机: Goods can be sold around the clock without staff. Japan has one of the highest vending-machine densities, with drink machines common on streets.
商店里读取银行卡并联网授权的终端，把收银、支付和库存记录连在一起。: A connected terminal reads payment cards and requests authorization, linking checkout, payment and inventory records.
收银的关键是让\"收到钱\"在付款那一刻就得到确认。把收银机联网，读卡后实时向发: Checkout needs confirmation that payment is accepted at the moment of sale. Networking the register lets it ask the issuing bank whether a card can pay and receive an answer within seconds ([[p:network|networks]]).
顾客刷卡、插卡或挥卡，终端读取卡号和芯片生成的一次性密码，经收单机构和 [[ca: A customer swipes, inserts or taps a card. The terminal sends card details and, for chip transactions, a one-time cryptogram through the acquirer and [[card-network|card network]] to the issuer. Approval produces a receipt and updates sales and inventory records.
20 世纪 70 年代，IBM、NCR 等公司把收银机接上计算机，形成电子 PO: IBM, NCR and others connected registers to computers in the 1970s, creating electronic POS systems. Dedicated card-authorization terminals spread through stores from the 1980s.
刷卡支付变得像付现金一样快，商店的销售、库存和会计数据融为一体；今天手机上的\": Card payments became as quick as cash, integrating sales, stock and accounting. Mobile collection codes and tablet registers continue these functions.
企业之间用标准格式的电子报文自动交换订单、发票和发货单，取代纸质单据。: Companies automatically exchange orders, invoices and shipping notices in standard electronic formats instead of paper.
两家企业交换订单如果靠纸张，每一份单据都要人工重新录入，既慢又容易出错。约定一套: Paper orders require each business to re-enter the same information, slowly and with errors. A shared electronic-message format ([[p:standard|standards]]) lets their computers read each other’s documents directly.
订单、发票、发货通知被编成固定字段的报文，比如\"商品编码、数量、交货日期\"，: Orders, invoices and dispatch notices use defined fields such as product code, quantity and delivery date. Private networks or the internet transmit them automatically, allowing suppliers to schedule production and shipments with little manual entry.
1948 年柏林空运期间，美军后勤人员吉尔伯特（Edward Guilbert）: Edward Guilbert’s standardized freight manifests during the 1948 Berlin Airlift are considered an early EDI precursor. US X12 and UN EDIFACT later became major standards.
沃尔玛等零售商用 EDI 把供应商连进自己的系统，库存周转大大加快，这是现代供应: Retailers such as Walmart connected suppliers through EDI, accelerating inventory turnover and providing a data foundation for modern supply chains and just-in-time management.
顾客自己扫码结账，或由摄像头和传感器自动识别拿走的商品，\"拿了就走\"。: Customers scan and pay themselves, or cameras and sensors identify products for automatic “just walk out” checkout.
结账的本质是\"确认顾客拿了什么\"。可以让顾客自己扫码，也可以让传感器自动看—: Checkout must establish what a customer took. Customers can scan items, or cameras and machine learning can infer selections and charge when sufficiently confident ([[p:probability|probabilistic inference]]).
自助收银机让顾客扫描条形码，同时用秤核对重量，防止漏扫。无人商店在货架上装摄像头: Self-checkout combines customer barcode scanning with weight checks. Automated stores use cameras and shelf-weight sensors, associate shoppers with accounts on entry and calculate charges from recorded selections on exit.
20 世纪 80 年代美国出现首批自助收银机；2018 年亚马逊在西雅图向公众开: Early self-checkout systems appeared in the United States in the 1980s. Amazon opened its first public Amazon Go walk-out store in Seattle in 2018.
自助收银在超市普及，节省了收银人手，但漏扫和盗损增加；全自动无人商店成本高，推广: Self-checkout spread across supermarkets, reducing cashier staffing but increasing missed scans and losses. Fully automated stores remain expensive and have spread more slowly than expected.
水印、安全线、光变油墨和塑料钞让伪钞越来越难造；1988 年澳大利亚发行首张流通: Watermarks, security threads, color-shifting inks and polymer notes make counterfeiting harder. Australia issued the first circulating polymer note in 1988.
防伪的思路是让\"真钞容易验、伪钞很难造\"：采用普通复印机和打印机无法复制的物: Security features aim to make genuine notes easy to check and counterfeits difficult to produce. Special paper, optical effects and microscopic structures resist ordinary copiers and printers ([[p:optics|optics]], [[p:structure|material structure]]).
水印和安全线在纸张制造时就嵌入；光变油墨换个角度会变色；凹版印刷让图案摸起来有凸: Watermarks and security threads are embedded during papermaking. Color-shifting ink changes with viewing angle, intaglio printing creates raised texture, and holograms and microprinting require precision equipment. Polymer notes can include transparent windows and last much longer than paper notes.
1988 年，澳大利亚发行了世界上第一张流通的塑料钞票，此后英国、加拿大等几十个: Australia issued the first circulating polymer banknote in 1988. Dozens of countries, including Britain and Canada, later adopted them.
伪钞的门槛被大大抬高；但随着移动支付普及，现金的使用越来越少，防伪的重心也从钞票: Counterfeiting became harder. As mobile payments expand and cash use declines, more security effort shifts toward digital systems.
先消费后还款的支付卡，背后是发卡行、收单行和卡组织组成的清算网络。: A card allows spending before repayment, supported by issuers, acquirers and card-network clearing systems.
信用卡的核心不是那张塑料卡，而是一张信任网络：商家不认识顾客，但相信发卡银行会付: A credit card’s core is a trust network. Merchants trust the issuing bank to pay, while banks rely on the network to coordinate transfers ([[p:network|network effects]]). More accepting merchants attract more cardholders, and vice versa.
刷卡时，商家的收单银行通过卡组织把请求发给发卡行，发卡行检查额度和风险后批准，整: The merchant’s acquiring bank routes an authorization request through the network to the issuer, which checks credit and risk, usually within seconds. Later clearing and settlement transfer payment to the merchant after fees of roughly 1–3%. Cardholders repay after billing; overdue balances can incur high interest.
1950 年，大来卡（Diners Club）成为第一张通用的签账卡；1958: Diners Club introduced a general-purpose charge card in 1950. Bank of America distributed BankAmericard widely in Fresno in 1958; it later became Visa. IBM developed magnetic-stripe technology in the 1960s, enabling machine-readable cards.
消费可以先买后付，零售和旅游业大为扩张；它也带来了消费债务问题。银行卡网络是后来: Buy-now-pay-later spending expanded retail and travel while creating consumer-debt problems. Card networks later underpinned online and mobile payments.
刷卡支付的\"四方模式\"：授权请求沿实线走一圈只要一两秒，真正的资金在之后批量: The four-party card model: authorization travels around the solid-arrow loop in a second or two, while actual funds move later through clearing and settlement.
Visa、万事达、银联等在银行之间传递授权和结算信息。: Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay and similar networks route authorization and settlement information between banks.
几千家银行如果两两签约，需要的协议数量会随银行数的平方增长；所有银行都接入一个中: If thousands of banks signed separate agreements with every other bank, the number of relationships would grow roughly with the square of the bank count. A shared central network lets each connect through one framework ([[p:network|networks]], [[p:standard|standards]]).
卡组织不放贷，只运营\"交换机\"：把授权请求从收单行转给发卡行，再在每天日终计: Card networks operate payment routing rather than issuing loans. They send requests from acquirers to issuers, calculate interbank obligations for clearing and establish rules for card numbering, security and fee allocation.
1958 年美国银行推出 BankAmericard，1976 年更名为 Vis: Bank of America launched BankAmericard in 1958; it became Visa in 1976. An association formed by banks in 1966 became Mastercard. China UnionPay was established in 2002 to enable domestic interbank card acceptance.
一张卡可以在全世界上千万家商户使用；卡组织也成为全球最赚钱的企业之一。: One card can work at tens of millions of merchants worldwide. Card networks also became highly profitable businesses.
让人不进银行也能取款，后来联网实现跨行取款。: Lets people withdraw cash outside a bank branch, with networking later enabling withdrawals across banks.
取钱的核心是验证身份和记账，柜员能做的判断，机器只要读卡、核对密码就能完成（[[: Cash withdrawal requires identity verification and account recording. A machine can perform routine checks by reading a card and verifying a PIN ([[p:network|networks]]).
插卡后，ATM 读取卡号，用户输入密码，机器把请求加密发给银行主机核对余额，批准: The ATM reads the card and accepts a PIN, then sends an encrypted request to the bank to check authorization and funds. A counting mechanism dispenses approved cash. Shared networks allow supported cards to use other banks’ machines.
1967 年 6 月，英国巴克莱银行在伦敦恩菲尔德安装了第一台现金取款机，由谢泼: Barclays installed an early cash dispenser in Enfield, London, in June 1967, designed by John Shepherd-Barron’s team. It used specially marked radioactive vouchers; personal identification numbers also became established through these systems.
银行\"下班后\"也能取钱，柜员从数钱转向理财销售；但在移动支付普及的国家，AT: Cash became available after branch hours, and tellers shifted toward other services. ATM numbers are declining in countries with widespread mobile payment.
用安全芯片代替磁条，每笔交易生成一次性密码，难以复制。: Replaces magnetic stripes with secure chips that generate transaction-specific cryptograms, making copying harder.
磁条上的数据是固定的，复制一份就能造出假卡。芯片里存着无法读出的密钥，每笔交易用: Magnetic-stripe data stays fixed and can be copied. A secure chip keeps a secret key internally and computes a one-time transaction cryptogram ([[p:oneway|one-way functions]]), so captured transaction data cannot simply authorize the next payment.
插卡或挥卡时，终端把交易金额、时间和一个随机数发给芯片，芯片用内部密钥生成\"交: For inserted or contactless cards, the terminal supplies transaction details and a random value. The chip uses its secret key to generate a cryptogram for the issuer to verify. The card is a small security computer designed to resist physical extraction of secrets.
1994 年，Europay、万事达和 Visa 三家开始联合发布 EMV 标准: Europay, Mastercard and Visa began the joint EMV standard initiative in 1994. Europe adopted chip cards earlier; the United States shifted widely in 2015.
伪卡盗刷大幅下降，欺诈转向了网上的\"无卡交易\"；手机 NFC 支付沿用了同样: Counterfeit-card fraud fell sharply, while fraud shifted toward card-not-present online transactions. Phone-based NFC payments use related principles.
全球银行间传递支付指令的标准化报文网络。: A standardized messaging network carries payment instructions between banks worldwide.
跨境汇款最大的难题不是运钱，而是让各国银行准确读懂彼此的指令。SWIFT 只传送: Cross-border payment depends on banks interpreting each other’s instructions correctly. SWIFT carries standardized electronic messages ([[p:standard|standards]]); the money itself remains recorded in bank accounts.
每家银行有一个 SWIFT 代码，汇款时发出格式固定的支付报文。由于两家银行之间: Banks use SWIFT identifiers and defined payment messages. If two banks lack a direct account relationship, funds may move through one or more correspondent banks. These chains help explain why some international transfers take days and incur substantial fees.
1973 年，200 多家银行在布鲁塞尔成立 SWIFT 协会，1977 年系统: More than 200 banks founded the SWIFT cooperative in Brussels in 1973. The system went live in 1977, replacing error-prone telex messages.
今天它连接 200 多个国家和地区的一万多家金融机构；被切断 SWIFT 连接也: It connects over 10,000 financial institutions in more than 200 countries and territories. Exclusion became a financial-sanctions tool, encouraging some countries to develop alternatives.
通过网页或 App 办理转账、查询等银行业务。: Banking services such as transfers and balance checks are performed through websites or apps.
银行业务本质上是修改账本上的数字，并不需要客户亲自到柜台；只要能安全地证明\"我: Many banking operations update numbers in a ledger rather than requiring a physical visit. If identity can be verified securely, instructions can arrive remotely ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
用户通过加密的 [[https-tls|HTTPS]] 连接登录，用密码加短信验: Customers connect through encrypted [[https-tls|HTTPS]], authenticate with passwords plus verification codes, security tokens or phone biometrics, then request information or transfers. Bank systems validate the instructions and update account records.
20 世纪 80 年代，英国和美国的银行就试验过用电视和电话线的终端办理业务；1: British and US banks experimented with television and telephone-line terminals in the 1980s. Stanford Federal Credit Union became an early internet-banking provider in 1994.
大部分银行业务从网点转到线上，银行网点大幅减少；纯线上的\"数字银行\"也随之出: Much banking activity moved online, reducing branch demand and enabling digital-only banks.
PayPal、支付宝等连接买家、商家和银行的网上支付服务，解决了网购的信任问题。: Services such as PayPal and Alipay connect buyers, merchants and banks, helping address trust in online shopping.
网购的难点在于互不认识的买卖双方都怕被骗。引入一个双方都信任的第三方，先收买家的: Unfamiliar buyers and sellers both fear fraud. A trusted intermediary can hold the buyer’s payment and release it after delivery, aligning incentives and reducing the trust problem ([[p:incentives|incentives and game theory]]).
买家在网站下单后跳转到支付平台，用银行卡或账户余额付款，平台通知商家发货。支付宝: After ordering, a buyer pays through a platform using a card or stored balance. The platform notifies the seller. Alipay’s escrow service temporarily holds funds until receipt is confirmed and provides dispute handling.
1998 年创立的 PayPal 让用户用电子邮件地址收付款，2002 年被 e: PayPal, founded in 1998, enabled payments using email addresses and was acquired by eBay in 2002. Alibaba introduced escrow for Taobao in 2003; Alipay became independently operated the next year.
网络零售得以爆发，中国的电子商务尤其依赖这一机制；支付平台积累的用户也为后来的: Online retail grew rapidly, particularly in China where escrow was important. Payment platforms’ user bases then supported [[mobile-payment|mobile payments]].
用手机扫码或 NFC 付款；中国的支付宝和微信支付让无现金社会率先成为现实。: Phones pay through QR codes or NFC. Alipay and WeChat Pay helped China rapidly adopt cashless payment.
移动支付是一个双边市场：用户越多，商家越愿意接受；商家越多，用户越愿意使用（[[: Mobile payment is a two-sided market: more users attract merchants, and more merchants attract users ([[p:network|network effects]]). Adoption can accelerate past a threshold ([[p:scale|scale effects]]). Low merchant cost was crucial in China: a printed QR code replaced dedicated card equipment.
① 扫码支付：用户用支付 App 扫商家的收款码，或者让商家扫自己手机上的付款码: ① QR payment: customers scan a merchant’s code or show their own payment code. The app sends the transaction to the provider, debits a balance or linked bank account and notifies both parties within seconds.
② NFC 支付：Apple Pay 等把银行卡变成手机里的一个\"代号\"（令: ② NFC payment: services such as Apple Pay replace the card number with a token on the phone. A tap authorizes payment without sharing the actual card number with the merchant.
③ 后台：支付机构与银行之间的资金往来，要经过统一的清算平台结算。: ③ Backend: transfers between payment providers and banks are cleared and settled through shared platforms.
2007 年肯尼亚推出的 [[m-pesa|M-Pesa]] 证明了手机可以当钱: Kenya’s [[m-pesa|M-Pesa]], launched in 2007, demonstrated phones as wallets. Alipay introduced barcode payment in 2011. WeChat added payments in 2013, and its 2014 Lunar New Year red envelopes encouraged tens of millions to link bank cards within days. Apple Pay launched in 2014.
中国在几年内跳过了信用卡普及阶段，进入以扫码为主的\"无现金社会\"，街边小贩也: China moved rapidly into QR-centered cashless payment without first developing universal credit-card use, including among street vendors. Transaction data supported online microlending and credit scoring. India’s UPI and Brazil’s Pix achieved broad adoption through publicly led infrastructure.
移动支付高度集中在少数平台，带来了数据隐私、垄断和老年人\"不会用\"的问题；各: Concentration in a few platforms raises privacy, competition and accessibility concerns, including difficulties for older users. Regulators have required shared clearing arrangements and continued cash acceptance.
扫码支付的一笔交易：信息流几秒内走完一圈，资金在后台的账户之间划转。右边是让它普: A QR-payment transaction: information completes its journey within seconds, while funds move between backend accounts. The right side shows the two-sided network effect supporting adoption.
肯尼亚用功能机短信转账的移动货币，让数千万没有银行账户的人获得金融服务。: Kenyan mobile money uses basic-phone messaging to transfer funds, providing financial services to millions without bank accounts.
很多人没有银行账户，但几乎人人都有手机。把话费账户变成\"电子钱\"，再用遍布乡: Many people lack bank accounts but have mobile phones. Electronic balances plus village agents for cash deposits and withdrawals ([[p:network|networks]]) let a phone number serve as a payment account.
用户在杂货店等代理点交现金，换成手机上的电子余额，再用功能机的短信菜单转给任何人: Users exchange cash for electronic balances at agents such as shops, then transfer funds through a basic phone’s messaging menu. Recipients withdraw cash at another agent. Neither a smartphone nor internet access is required.
2007 年，肯尼亚电信运营商 Safaricom 与沃达丰推出 M-Pesa（: Safaricom and Vodafone launched M-Pesa in Kenya in 2007. “Pesa” means money in Swahili.
几年内就覆盖了肯尼亚大多数成年人；城市打工者能把钱即时汇回家乡。研究估计它帮助约: Within a few years it reached most Kenyan adults, allowing urban workers to send money home immediately. Research estimated it helped about 2% of Kenyan households escape poverty.
7×24 小时秒级到账的银行间支付网络，如印度 UPI 和巴西 Pix。: Interbank networks such as India’s UPI and Brazil’s Pix deliver payments within seconds, around the clock.
传统转账慢，是因为银行间批量轧差、隔天结算。如果央行或公共机构建一条 7×24: Traditional transfers can be slow because banks net and settle batches later. Shared infrastructure operating 24/7 connects banks and apps under common standards ([[p:standard|shared standards]]), allowing near-immediate transfers.
用户用手机号、二维码或别名发起付款，指令经过中央平台实时通知收款银行，资金立即入: Users pay through phone numbers, QR codes or aliases. A central platform routes the instruction immediately to the recipient’s bank, enabling rapid credit. Broad access for banks and payment apps supports very low or zero fees.
英国 2008 年上线\"快速支付\"；2016 年印度推出统一支付接口（UPI: Britain introduced Faster Payments in 2008. India launched UPI in 2016, Brazil’s central bank introduced Pix in 2020, and the United States launched FedNow in 2023.
印度 UPI 每月处理上百亿笔交易，巴西 Pix 迅速成为最常用的支付方式；公共: India’s UPI handles over ten billion transactions monthly, while Brazil’s Pix quickly became a leading payment method. Competition between public infrastructure and private platforms is a new focus of payment policy.
用统计模型把一个人的还款记录变成一个分数，决定能否贷款和利率高低。: Statistical models turn repayment history into a score used in lending decisions and interest-rate setting.
银行无法看透一个人，但可以看他过去的行为：按时还款的人，将来按时还款的概率也更高: Banks cannot know a person’s future, but past repayment behavior provides statistical evidence about future repayment ([[p:probability|probability and statistics]]). Models compress this complex history into a credit score.
模型考察还款记录、负债比例、信用历史长短、新开账户数等，用历史数据拟合违约概率，: Models consider payment history, debt utilization, length of credit history and newly opened accounts. Historical data estimates default probability, which is converted into a score used in approval and pricing.
1956 年费尔（Bill Fair）和艾萨克（Earl Isaac）创立 Fa: Bill Fair and Earl Isaac founded Fair Isaac in 1956. Its FICO score, introduced in 1989, became a common US consumer-credit standard.
贷款审批从信贷员的主观判断变成几秒钟的自动决策，信贷大规模扩张；但模型可能放大历: Decisions shifted from individual judgment toward rapid automated assessment, expanding credit. Models can also reproduce historical biases and disadvantage people without credit histories.
用规则和机器学习实时识别可疑交易。: Rules and machine learning identify suspicious transactions in real time.
正常交易有规律，欺诈交易往往偏离规律。用历史数据学习\"正常\"的样子，对每笔新: Fraud often differs from ordinary transaction patterns. Models learn typical behavior and score each new transaction’s risk ([[p:probability|probability]]), blocking or requesting further verification above a threshold.
系统在几十毫秒内检查交易的金额、地点、设备、时间和商户类型，结合规则和机器学习模: Within tens of milliseconds, systems assess amount, location, device, time and merchant type using rules and machine learning. A card used in two countries minutes apart may trigger a block or additional verification.
20 世纪 90 年代起，银行开始用神经网络监控信用卡交易；移动支付时代，平台的: Banks began using neural networks to monitor card transactions in the 1990s. Mobile-payment platforms now assess hundreds of millions of transactions daily.
盗刷损失被控制在交易额的很小比例；风控的难点是平衡——拦得太严会误伤正常用户，太: Fraud losses can be kept to a small fraction of payment volume. The challenge is balancing missed fraud against false alarms that inconvenience legitimate customers.
在用户授权下通过 API 共享银行数据，让第三方开发理财和支付服务。: With customer authorization, APIs share bank data so third parties can provide financial-management and payment services.
用户的银行数据属于用户本人。用统一的接口标准（[[p:standard|标准]]: Open banking treats customers as entitled to control access to their banking data. Standard interfaces ([[p:standard|standards]]) let authorized third parties read account information or initiate payments, making banks accessible as platforms.
银行按规定提供标准化的 [[api|API]]，第三方应用获得用户授权后，可以读: Banks provide standardized [[api|APIs]]. Authorized apps can combine balances and transaction histories from several banks or initiate transfers. Access can be revoked without requiring customers to give third parties their banking passwords.
2018 年 1 月，欧盟第二版《支付服务指令》（PSD2）开始实施，英国的\": The EU’s second Payment Services Directive, PSD2, took effect in January 2018, alongside the UK’s Open Banking standards.
记账、比价、借贷等应用可以跨银行整合数据，银行的竞争更加激烈；澳大利亚、巴西等国: Budgeting, comparison and lending apps can integrate data across banks, increasing competition. Australia, Brazil and others introduced related frameworks.
用磁性墨水把账号印在支票上，计算机就能自动读取和分拣，银行由此率先进入计算机时代: Magnetic ink prints account information on checks for automated reading and sorting, helping banks adopt computers early.
计算机要处理支票，首先得\"读得懂\"支票。用含氧化铁的磁性墨水印出特定字体的数: Computers first needed a reliable way to read checks. Special digits printed in iron-oxide-containing ink produce distinctive signals at a magnetic head ([[p:induction|electromagnetic induction]]), remaining readable despite many stains or stamps.
支票底部用磁墨印上银行代码和账号。读取机先给字符磁化，再让磁头读出波形，识别后自: Bank and account codes appear in magnetic ink along the check’s bottom. Readers magnetize the characters, recognize their magnetic waveforms, sort checks by bank and support account posting.
1959 年，美国银行与斯坦福研究所合作的 ERMA 系统交付使用，同期美国银行: The ERMA system, developed by Bank of America and Stanford Research Institute, entered service in 1959. Around the same time, the American Bankers Association adopted magnetic-ink character recognition, MICR.
每天数以百万计的支票实现自动处理，银行成为最早大规模使用计算机的行业之一；MIC: Millions of checks could be processed automatically each day, making banking an early large-scale computer user. MICR characters remain on checks today.
银行之间先汇总轧差、再在央行账户上最终划拨资金；ACH 批量处理小额，RTGS: Banks calculate obligations and settle through central-bank accounts. ACH handles retail payments in batches; RTGS settles large payments individually in real time.
如果银行之间每笔转账都实际划拨，需要的资金量非常大。把一天里互相的应收应付先抵消: Funding every interbank transfer separately requires substantial liquidity. Offsetting mutual obligations and settling only the net amount ([[p:network|networks]]) reduces this need. For large payments, individual real-time settlement reduces certain settlement risks.
清算是算清\"谁该付谁多少\"，结算是最终在央行账户上划转资金。小额支付通过自动: Clearing calculates who owes what; settlement transfers the final funds. Automated clearing houses, ACH, batch smaller payments. Real-time gross settlement, RTGS, processes large payments individually and immediately, reducing the risk of unsettled obligations.
1974 年德国赫斯塔特银行倒闭时，交易对手已付出马克却没收到美元，这种\"时差: When Germany’s Herstatt Bank failed in 1974, counterparties had paid deutsche marks but had not received dollars. The resulting foreign-exchange settlement risk became known as Herstatt risk. Countries subsequently expanded RTGS systems.
清算和结算系统是整个金融体系的\"心脏\"，一旦停转，经济活动就会瘫痪，所以由央: Clearing and settlement form the financial system’s core infrastructure. Disruption can halt economic activity, so central banks operate or closely supervise them.
纳斯达克成为首个电子报价市场，交易从交易大厅喊价转向计算机撮合。: Nasdaq became the first electronic quotation market, helping move trading from shouted floor orders toward computer matching.
交易的本质是撮合：把愿意买的价格和愿意卖的价格配对。这是一种纯粹的信息处理，计算: Trading matches buyers’ and sellers’ prices. This information-processing task can be performed by computers faster and more cheaply, with transparent rules ([[p:network|networks]]).
买卖双方通过经纪商把订单发到交易所的撮合引擎，引擎维护一份\"订单簿\"，按价格: Brokers send orders to an exchange’s matching engine. Its order book matches them under rules such as price priority followed by time priority, then distributes updated prices. Much trading now completes within milliseconds, leaving floors with a largely symbolic and broadcast role.
1971 年 2 月，纳斯达克作为世界上第一个电子报价市场开业；1986 年伦敦: Nasdaq opened as the first electronic quotation market in February 1971. London’s 1986 Big Bang reforms replaced floor-based practices with electronic dealing. US stocks adopted decimal pricing in 2001, sharply narrowing spreads.
交易成本大降，普通人也能通过网络便宜地买卖股票；但它也为 [[high-freq: Lower costs made online stock trading accessible to ordinary investors. It also enabled [[high-frequency-trading|high-frequency trading]], making markets faster and sometimes more fragile.
用数学模型给期权等金融衍生品定价，并用程序执行交易策略。: Mathematical models price derivatives such as options, while software executes trading strategies.
股价的短期变化很像随机游走（[[p:probability|概率]]），但随机并: Short-term stock-price changes can be modeled as random walks ([[p:probability|probability]]). Randomness can still be analyzed: option value depends on the range of possible underlying-price movements. Under a model’s assumptions, a portfolio replicating an option’s payoff can be used to derive its fair price.
布莱克—斯科尔斯公式输入股价、行权价、到期时间、利率和波动率，就给出期权价格。量: The Black–Scholes formula takes stock price, strike price, time to expiry, interest rate and volatility as inputs. Quantitative funds extend statistical modeling to identifying patterns and executing trades automatically.
1900 年，法国的巴舍利耶首次用随机游走描述股价；1973 年布莱克（Fisc: Louis Bachelier modeled stock prices as random walks in 1900. Fischer Black and Myron Scholes published their option-pricing formula in 1973, with Robert Merton extending the theory. Scholes and Merton received the 1997 economics Nobel; Black had died in 1995.
期权、互换等衍生品市场迅速膨胀，金融变成了数学和计算的行业；但模型假设一旦失效，: Options, swaps and other derivatives expanded rapidly, making finance increasingly mathematical and computational. When assumptions fail, losses can be amplified, as illustrated by Long-Term Capital Management’s collapse in 1998.
用算法在微秒级内大量买卖，靠极小价差和速度优势获利。: Algorithms trade at microsecond timescales, seeking small price differences and speed advantages.
在电子市场中，同一个价格谁先下单谁先成交。信号在光纤中传播也需要时间（[[p:l: For orders at the same price, earlier arrival often wins priority. Signals take time to travel through fiber ([[p:locality|locality and latency]]), so servers closer to an exchange can gain microseconds and capture small price differences.
交易公司把服务器托管在交易所机房旁边，用专用芯片和极简程序在微秒内下单撤单。为了: Firms colocate servers near exchanges and use specialized chips and streamlined code to place or cancel orders rapidly. Some built straighter fiber routes or microwave links between trading centers to reduce transmission time.
2000 年代后期，高频交易已占美国股票成交量的一大半；2010 年 5 月的\: By the late 2000s, high-frequency trading accounted for much of US equity volume. During the May 2010 Flash Crash, the Dow fell nearly a thousand points within minutes before rapidly recovering.
买卖价差缩小，交易成本下降；但关于它是否公平、是否加剧了市场的脆弱性，至今仍有争: Spreads narrowed and trading costs fell. Debate continues over fairness and whether high-speed trading increases market fragility.
用算法根据风险偏好自动配置和再平衡指数基金组合，把理财门槛降到很低。: Algorithms allocate and rebalance index-fund portfolios according to risk preferences, lowering access costs for investment management.
多数投资者跑不赢市场，长期来看，分散持有低费率的指数基金、按时再平衡更划算（[[: Robo-advice draws on diversified, low-cost index investing and periodic rebalancing ([[p:optimization|optimization]]). These rules can be implemented in software rather than requiring expensive personal advisory services.
用户在线回答年龄、收入、投资期限和风险承受能力等问题，算法据此给出股票和债券的配: Users answer questions about age, income, investment horizon and risk tolerance. Algorithms suggest stock–bond allocations and purchase index funds, then rebalance when market movements alter proportions. Some systems also automate tax management.
2010 年美国的 Betterment 上线，随后 Wealthfront 等: Betterment launched in the United States in 2010, followed by firms such as Wealthfront. Traditional asset managers soon introduced their own automated advisory services.
理财顾问的服务门槛从几十万美元降到几乎为零，费率只有传统顾问的几分之一；但算法无: Minimum investment requirements fell from hundreds of thousands of dollars to very little, with fees a fraction of traditional advisory charges. Algorithms do not replace human reassurance during market panic.
通过网络平台向大量普通人小额募资或借款，绕开银行和风投；P2P 网贷因风险失控在: Online platforms raise small contributions or loans from many people outside traditional bank and venture funding. Uncontrolled P2P-lending risks prompted crackdowns in several countries.
一个项目向少数几个大投资人要钱很难，向成千上万人每人要一点就容易得多（[[p:n: Finding a few large investors can be difficult; collecting small amounts from thousands of supporters offers another route ([[p:network|networks]]). The internet greatly reduces the cost of reaching them.
发起人在平台上展示项目和回报，支持者小额出资，有的换取产品，有的换取股权或利息；: Creators present projects and proposed rewards, products, equity or interest. Some campaigns collect funds only if a target is met and otherwise refund commitments. Peer-to-peer lending platforms directly match borrowers and lenders.
2005 年，小额贷款平台 Kiva 和英国 P2P 网贷平台 Zopa 先后上: Kiva and Britain’s Zopa launched in 2005. Kickstarter popularized reward- and preorder-based crowdfunding from 2009.
独立游戏、硬件创业和公益项目有了新的融资渠道；但中国的 P2P 网贷因资金池、虚: Independent games, hardware startups and charitable projects gained new funding channels. China phased out P2P lending around 2020 after widespread pooled-fund abuses, fake projects and platform failures.
中本聪设计的去中心化数字货币，用工作量证明让陌生人不依赖银行就能就账本达成一致。: Satoshi Nakamoto’s decentralized digital currency uses proof of work to coordinate a ledger without relying on banks.
数字文件可以无限复制，所以数字货币最大的难题是\"双重支付\"——同一笔钱被花两: Digital information can be copied, creating the double-spending problem. Banks traditionally prevent it through a central ledger. Bitcoin distributes a public ledger across thousands of nodes and uses a computational competition to add blocks. Rewriting confirmed history requires substantial competing computational power, with incentives intended to make attacks costly ([[p:incentives|incentives and game theory]], [[p:oneway|one-way functions]]).
① 交易：每个账户是一对密钥，转账要用私钥签名，任何人都能用公钥验证。: ① Transactions: private keys sign transfers, and corresponding public keys allow verification.
② 挖矿：矿工把新交易打包成区块，不断尝试不同的随机数，直到区块的 [[hash: ② Mining: miners package transactions into blocks and try different nonces until the [[hashing|hash]] falls below a target. Successful miners receive newly issued coins. Difficulty adjusts roughly every two weeks to maintain an average block interval near ten minutes.
③ 发行：奖励大约每四年减半，总量上限为 2100 万枚。: ③ Issuance: the block subsidy halves approximately every four years, with total issuance capped at 21 million coins.
2008 年 10 月 31 日，化名\"中本聪\"（Satoshi Nakam: The pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto published the Bitcoin white paper on October 31, 2008, and generated the first block on January 3, 2009. A May 2010 purchase of two pizzas for 10,000 bitcoins became a famous early physical-goods transaction. Nakamoto’s identity remains unknown.
比特币证明了在没有中央机构的情况下，陌生人也能就一本账达成一致，由此引出了 [[: Bitcoin demonstrated decentralized ledger agreement, inspiring [[blockchain|blockchain]] and the cryptocurrency industry. Its volatile price has made it more commonly a speculative asset or “digital gold” than everyday money. The United States approved spot Bitcoin ETFs in 2024.
工作量证明的耗电量相当于一个中等国家，加上被用于勒索和洗钱，比特币一直饱受争议。: Proof of work consumes electricity on the scale of a medium-sized country. Energy use and applications in ransomware and money laundering remain controversial.
挖矿就是\"猜数字\"：只能一次次地试，直到哈希值足够小；验证答案却只需算一次。: Mining repeatedly guesses values until a hash meets the target; checking a proposed answer takes just one calculation. Below is the roughly four-year block-reward halving schedule.
用哈希把一个个记账区块串成链，由众多节点共同维护，难以篡改历史。: Links transaction blocks with hashes and distributes copies across nodes, making past records difficult to alter.
哈希函数能把任意数据变成一个固定长度的\"指纹\"，数据改动一个字，指纹就完全不: A hash maps data to a fixed-length fingerprint, with tiny changes producing very different results ([[p:oneway|one-way functions]]). Each block records its predecessor’s hash, linking the sequence. Altering an earlier block requires rebuilding subsequent records. Distributed copies and consensus ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]) make unauthorized changes difficult.
① 结构：每个区块包括区块头和一批交易，区块头里有前一个区块的哈希、本区块交易的: ① Structure: a block contains a header and transactions. The header includes the previous block’s hash, a Merkle root summarizing current transactions and a timestamp.
② 共识：节点按照 [[consensus-algorithm|共识规则]]决定: ② Consensus: nodes follow [[consensus-algorithm|consensus rules]] to accept new blocks. In proof-of-work chains, competing branches are resolved by accumulated work.
③ 两种类型：公有链人人可以参与；联盟链只让经过许可的机构参与，速度更快，但更接: ③ Types: public chains permit broad participation. Consortium chains restrict participation to authorized organizations and often achieve higher speed while resembling conventional databases more closely.
1991 年，哈伯（Stuart Haber）和斯托内塔（W. Scott St: Stuart Haber and W. Scott Stornetta proposed hash-linked document timestamps in 1991. Bitcoin’s 2008 white paper combined related ideas with proof of work to create a decentralized blockchain.
区块链让\"不需要信任中心的共享账本\"成为可能，催生了 [[smart-con: Shared ledgers without a single trusted operator enabled [[smart-contract|smart contracts]], stablecoins and digital assets. A blockchain boom around 2017 produced many projects later found to need only conventional databases. Major uses remain concentrated in crypto-assets and cross-border settlement.
\"上链\"的数据只能保证不被篡改，不能保证一开始就是真的；公有链的性能和能耗也: A blockchain can make recorded data difficult to alter; it cannot establish whether the original input was true. Public-chain performance and energy use remain constraints.
区块通过\"前一块的哈希\"串成链。篡改区块 2 的一笔交易，它的哈希就变了，区: Blocks link through the previous block’s hash. Changing a transaction in block 2 changes its hash, which no longer matches the fingerprint stored in block 3, revealing the broken link.
记账权给\"算力最多\"或\"押币最多\"的人，让作恶的代价高于收益。: Allocates block-production influence through computational work or staked assets, aiming to make misconduct more costly than its rewards.
在人人都可以匿名加入的网络里，按\"人头\"投票会被假账号操纵。改成按某种昂贵的: Anonymous open networks cannot safely count accounts as votes because fake identities are cheap. Weighting participation by costly resources—computational work or pledged coins—raises attack costs ([[p:incentives|incentives and game theory]]).
工作量证明要求记账者反复计算哈希，找到满足条件的答案，作恶需要掌握全网多数算力；: Proof of work requires repeated hashing to find an acceptable result, with major attacks requiring substantial network hash power. Proof of stake requires validators to pledge tokens that can be penalized for specified misconduct, using far less electricity.
1997 年，亚当·拜克（Adam Back）提出用于防垃圾邮件的 Hashca: Adam Back proposed Hashcash against spam in 1997, influencing Bitcoin. Ethereum switched from proof of work to proof of stake in September 2022, cutting energy use by roughly 99.9%.
两种机制分别代表\"用电换安全\"和\"用资本换安全\"；挖矿也催生了专用芯片和: The approaches trade electricity or committed capital for security incentives. Mining also created industries for dedicated chips and large facilities.
部署在区块链上自动执行的程序，以太坊让区块链从记账扩展到通用计算。: Programs executed on a blockchain extend ledgers into programmable systems, as demonstrated by Ethereum.
很多合同条款都是\"如果……就……\"的规则，可以写成程序。程序部署在区块链上后: Many contractual rules have an if–then structure that software can express. Blockchain participants execute shared code and agree on the result, reducing reliance on one party’s unilateral control ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]], [[p:incentives|incentives]]).
开发者用 Solidity 等语言编写合约，部署到以太坊上获得一个地址。用户向这: Developers write contracts in languages such as Solidity and deploy them to an address. Users call them through transactions. Computation requires gas fees to constrain resource use and endless loops. Contracts can hold funds and interact with other contracts.
1994 年，萨博（Nick Szabo）用自动售货机作比喻提出\"智能合约\": Nick Szabo introduced smart contracts in 1994 using vending machines as an analogy. Vitalik Buterin proposed Ethereum in 2013; it launched in July 2015. An exploit drained substantial funds from The DAO in 2016, leading to a contentious hard fork that reversed its consequences on the resulting Ethereum branch.
区块链从单纯记账扩展为可编程平台，催生了 [[defi|去中心化金融]]、NFT: Blockchains became programmable platforms supporting [[defi|decentralized finance]], NFTs and tokens. Irreversible execution can also make software bugs costly, creating demand for contract security audits.
与美元等法币挂钩的加密货币，用于链上结算和跨境转账。: Cryptographic tokens linked to currencies such as the US dollar, used for blockchain settlement and cross-border transfers.
加密货币价格波动太大，不适合当钱用。发行方每发行一枚代币，就在银行存放 1 美元: Volatile cryptocurrency prices complicate payment use. Reserve-backed stablecoins aim to hold one dollar or equivalent safe assets for each dollar token and support one-for-one redemption, anchoring the price ([[p:incentives|incentives and trust]]).
用户把美元交给发行方，换得链上代币，可以在区块链上 7×24 小时转账；赎回时代: Users provide dollars to an issuer in return for tokens transferable around the clock. Redemption destroys the corresponding tokens. Algorithmic stablecoins instead try to regulate supply without equivalent reserves, an approach that has proved fragile.
2014 年，泰达币（USDT）发行；2022 年 5 月，算法稳定币 Terr: Tether’s USDT launched in 2014. TerraUSD lost its peg in May 2022, wiping out tens of billions of dollars in market value within days. In July 2025, the United States signed the GENIUS Act, its first federal stablecoin law, with reserve and disclosure requirements.
稳定币成为加密市场的主要结算工具，也被用于跨境转账；储备是否真实充足，是监管的焦: Stablecoins became major settlement tools in crypto markets and are used for cross-border transfers. Whether reserves are real and sufficient remains a central regulatory concern.
用智能合约实现借贷、交易等金融服务，无需传统中介，但风险和漏洞频发。: Smart contracts provide lending and trading without traditional intermediaries, but exploits and other risks are frequent.
借贷、交易等金融服务的规则可以写成智能合约，代替银行和交易所来执行（[[p:in: Financial rules can be encoded in smart contracts that perform functions otherwise handled by banks or exchanges ([[p:incentives|incentives and game theory]]). Open protocols can allow broad participation and public inspection of code.
去中心化交易所用\"自动做市商\"代替订单簿，资金池里两种代币的数量乘积保持不变: Some decentralized exchanges use automated market makers instead of order books, with a constant-product relationship between two pooled token balances determining prices. Lending protocols often require excess collateral and automatically liquidate positions below specified thresholds.
2017 年，MakerDAO 推出超额抵押的稳定币 DAI；2018 年 Un: MakerDAO introduced the overcollateralized DAI stablecoin in 2017. Uniswap launched in 2018. Large inflows during summer 2020 became known as “DeFi Summer.”
它展示了无须许可的金融系统的可能性；但黑客攻击、合约漏洞和投机泡沫频发，每年被盗: DeFi demonstrates permissionless financial infrastructure, but hacks, contract flaws and speculative bubbles recur, with annual thefts measured in billions of dollars.
在区块链上登记的独一无二的数字凭证，2021 年曾一度炒作火热。: A uniquely identified digital certificate registered on a blockchain, subject to intense speculation in 2021.
同质化代币就像钞票，每一张都可以互换；非同质化代币给每个代币一个独一无二的编号（: Fungible tokens are interchangeable like currency units. Non-fungible tokens have unique identifiers ([[p:oneway|one-way functions]]) and ownership records used to represent digital works or assets.
创作者在智能合约中\"铸造\" NFT，记录编号、所有者和一个指向作品的链接；交: Creators mint NFTs through contracts that record an identifier, owner and often a link to a work. Trades transfer the on-chain ownership record. The image itself is usually stored elsewhere and remains technically copyable.
2017 年的游戏\"加密猫\"（CryptoKitties）一度挤爆以太坊；2: CryptoKitties congested Ethereum in 2017. In March 2021, Christie’s sold a digital work by Beeple for about $69 million.
2021 年 NFT 交易火爆，2022 年后交易量和价格暴跌；它也引发了关于数: NFT trading surged in 2021, followed by sharp price and volume declines after 2022. The boom prompted debate about digital ownership and copyright.
由中央银行发行的数字形式法定货币，如数字人民币。: Digital legal tender issued by a central bank, such as the digital renminbi.
现金是央行直接对公众的负债，而银行存款和支付平台余额是私人机构的负债。CBDC: Cash is a direct central-bank liability, unlike commercial-bank deposits or private payment balances. A CBDC makes central-bank money digital ([[p:network|networks]]), preserving public access to this form of money as cash use declines.
数字人民币采用\"双层运营\"：央行发行，商业银行负责兑换和服务，用户通过 Ap: The digital renminbi uses a two-tier arrangement: the central bank issues it, while commercial banks handle exchange and services. App wallets support payments, including some phone-to-phone offline functions. Its design seeks managed anonymity, balancing small-payment privacy with anti-money-laundering requirements.
2020 年 10 月，巴哈马发行了第一种全国性的央行数字货币\"沙元\"；同年: The Bahamas launched the nationwide Sand Dollar in October 2020. China began digital-renminbi pilots in cities including Shenzhen that year. The European Central Bank has also been preparing a digital euro.
各国央行借此重新思考货币形态；但它的使用率普遍不高，隐私和对商业银行的冲击也引发: CBDCs prompt central banks to reconsider money’s form. Adoption has generally been limited, while privacy and potential effects on commercial banks remain debated.
它是服役最久的载人飞船；2011 年到 2020 年间是往返国际空间站的唯一载人: It is the longest-serving crewed spacecraft. Between 2011 and 2020, it was the only vehicle carrying people to and from the International Space Station. China’s Shenzhou spacecraft adopted a similar three-module layout.
把石灰石和黏土烧成熟料再磨粉，加水后硬化成\"人造石\"；它也是主要碳排放来源之: Limestone and clay are fired into clinker and ground into powder that hardens with water into artificial stone. Cement is also a major carbon-emission source.
石灰石在高温下分解出氧化钙，与黏土中的硅、铝结合成新矿物；加水后这些矿物发生水化: Heat decomposes limestone into calcium oxide, which reacts with silicon and aluminum from clay to form new minerals. Adding water triggers hydration, growing interlocking crystals that bind aggregate together—a controlled rearrangement of [[p:bond|chemical bonds]].
石灰石和黏土磨细混合，在回转窑中烧到约 1450 摄氏度，形成小块的\"熟料\": Finely ground limestone and clay are mixed and heated to about 1,450°C in a rotary kiln, producing clinker. Cooling and grinding it with a little gypsum makes cement. Cement + sand + stone + water = concrete.
1824 年英国砖瓦匠约瑟夫·阿斯普丁（Joseph Aspdin）获得\"波特: British bricklayer Joseph Aspdin patented Portland cement in 1824, naming it after the hardened material’s resemblance to stone from the Isle of Portland. Modern high-temperature clinker cement developed in the 1840s.
混凝土成为人类用量最大的人造材料。代价是碳排放：煅烧石灰石本身就会释放二氧化碳，: Concrete became humanity’s most-used manufactured material. Limestone decomposition and fuel combustion make cement responsible for roughly 7–8% of global carbon-dioxide emissions (see [[green-steel]]).
混凝土抗压、钢筋抗拉，两者热膨胀系数接近，结合在一起取长补短。: Concrete resists compression and steel reinforcement carries tension. Similar thermal expansion helps them work together.
混凝土像石头一样**抗压**很强、**抗拉**却很弱，约只有抗压强度的十分之一；: Concrete is strong in **compression** but weak in **tension**, with tensile strength roughly one-tenth of compressive strength. Steel reinforcement supplies tensile capacity where the concrete is stretched ([[p:stress|stress]]).
更妙的是三点巧合：钢和混凝土的热膨胀系数几乎相同，冷热变化时不会互相撕裂；混凝土: Three properties support the combination: steel and concrete expand at similar rates with temperature; they bond well; and alkaline concrete helps protect embedded steel from corrosion ([[p:structure|structure determines properties]]).
一根横梁受压弯曲时，上半部分被挤压、下半部分被拉伸。所以梁的底部要多放钢筋，柱子: In a beam bending under downward load, the upper region compresses and the lower region stretches, so more reinforcement is placed below. Columns use longitudinal bars and restraining ties. Construction typically assembles reinforcement and formwork, places and compacts concrete, then cures it toward its specified strength over roughly four weeks.
1867 年法国园艺师约瑟夫·莫尼耶（Joseph Monier）为铁丝加固的混: French gardener Joseph Monier patented wire-reinforced concrete flowerpots in 1867, later extending the idea to pipes and bridges. François Hennebique patented an integrated reinforced-concrete beam-and-column system in 1892, helping establish it as a general building method.
钢筋混凝土便宜、可塑、耐火，几乎可以浇成任何形状，从住宅楼、桥梁、大坝到核电站安: Inexpensive, moldable and fire-resistant, reinforced concrete can take almost any shape and appears in homes, bridges, dams and nuclear containment buildings.
钢筋混凝土并非永久耐用。空气中的二氧化碳会慢慢渗入、降低混凝土的碱性，海边的氯盐: Reinforced concrete is not permanent. Carbon dioxide gradually reduces its alkalinity, while chloride salts can penetrate near coasts. Corroding steel expands and cracks the concrete. Structures are therefore commonly designed for service lives of roughly 50–100 years.
一根受弯的梁：上部受压交给混凝土，下部受拉交给钢筋。右侧是让两者能\"合作\"的: A bending beam: concrete carries upper compression and steel carries lower tension. The right side shows three conditions that make them compatible.
浇筑前或后拉紧钢筋，预先给混凝土加压，让它能跨越更长距离。: Tensions steel before or after casting to pre-compress concrete, allowing longer spans.
既然混凝土怕拉，就在它受力之前先把它\"挤紧\"；使用时荷载产生的拉力先要抵消这: Because concrete is vulnerable in tension, compress it before loading. Service loads must first offset that pre-compression, helping keep the concrete compressed ([[p:stress|stress]]).
**先张法**在浇筑前把高强钢绞线拉紧，混凝土硬化后再放松，钢绞线回缩把混凝土压: **Pre-tensioning** stretches high-strength strands before casting; releasing them after hardening compresses the concrete. **Post-tensioning** leaves ducts in the concrete, then tensions and anchors tendons after it hardens.
法国工程师欧仁·弗雷西内（Eugène Freyssinet）1928 年取得预: French engineer Eugène Freyssinet patented prestressed concrete in 1928. It spread widely in bridge construction after World War II.
同样的截面，预应力梁能跨越更长距离、裂缝更少，今天的高架桥、大跨楼板和核电站安全: For a given section, prestressing allows longer spans and fewer cracks. It is widely used in viaducts, long-span floors and nuclear containment structures.
用钢梁钢柱组成骨架承重，外墙只是\"挂\"上去的，建筑得以向高空发展。: A load-bearing steel skeleton allows exterior walls to hang from the frame, enabling taller buildings.
钢的强度重量比远高于砖石，用钢梁钢柱组成骨架承受全部重量，外墙就不必承重，可以做: Steel has a much higher strength-to-weight ratio than masonry. A beam-and-column skeleton carries the building, leaving thin, lightweight exterior walls and removing the height constraint imposed by thick load-bearing walls below ([[p:stress|stress and material strength]]).
竖向的钢柱把楼层重量传到地基，横向的钢梁托起楼板，梁柱之间用螺栓或焊接连接；为了: Columns transfer floor loads to foundations; beams support floors, joined by bolts or welds. Bracing or rigid joints resist wind and earthquake forces. Steel weakens rapidly at elevated fire temperatures, so protective coatings or concrete encasement are needed.
1885 年芝加哥建成的家庭保险大楼（Home Insurance Buildi: Chicago’s Home Insurance Building, designed by William Le Baron Jenney and completed in 1885, used extensive metal framing and is often called the first skyscraper. Cheaper steel from the [[bessemer-process|Bessemer process]] helped make tall steel buildings feasible.
钢结构催生了\"芝加哥学派\"和摩天大楼，也让工厂、体育馆和机场可以获得巨大的无: Steel frames supported the Chicago School and skyscrapers and created large column-free spaces in factories, stadiums and airports.
钢结构 + 安全电梯 + 抗风设计，让城市向天空要空间。: Steel frames, safety elevators and wind engineering let cities expand upward.
盖高楼要同时解决三件事：承重、抗风、上下楼。楼越高，重量按高度累加压向底部，而风: Tall buildings must carry weight, resist wind and transport people vertically. Gravity loads accumulate toward the base, while wind’s overturning effect rises more rapidly with height. For supertall buildings, **wind can be harder to manage than gravity** ([[p:squarecube|square–cube law]], [[p:stress|stress]]).
现代超高层通常用钢筋混凝土\"核心筒\"（电梯井和楼梯间围成的筒体）加外围钢或混: Supertall towers commonly combine a reinforced-concrete core around lifts and stairs with a perimeter frame. Outrigger trusses link them, resisting bending like a hollow bamboo stem.
为了让风\"抓不住\"楼体，设计者会把外形做成逐层收进、扭转或开槽，打乱风在背后: Setbacks, twists and openings disrupt regular wind vortices behind a tower. Some buildings suspend tuned mass dampers weighing hundreds of tons near the top; their opposing motion reduces sway.
高楼还离不开 [[elevator|安全电梯]]、加压供水、防火分区和避难层。: Tall buildings also need [[elevator|safety elevators]], pressurized water supplies, fire compartments and refuge floors.
1885 年芝加哥家庭保险大楼开启了摩天大楼时代；1931 年纽约帝国大厦高 3: Chicago’s 1885 Home Insurance Building began the skyscraper era. New York’s 381-meter Empire State Building, completed in 1931, held the height record for roughly forty years. Dubai’s 828-meter Burj Khalifa opened in 2010 and remains the tallest in the manuscript’s account; its Y-shaped plan helps resist wind. Taipei 101 contains a tuned mass damper of roughly 660 tons.
摩天大楼让城市在有限的土地上容纳更多人和办公空间，地价最高的城市中心由此向上生长: Skyscrapers accommodate more people and offices on limited land, especially in high-value city centers. They also symbolize competition between cities and countries.
楼越高，电梯井、结构和设备占用的面积比例越大，每平方米的造价也越高。所以超高层往: As height increases, elevators, structure and equipment consume a larger floor-area share, while construction cost per square meter rises. Supertall projects often reflect symbolic ambitions as well as economics.
超高层的受力：重力向下累加，风从侧面推，核心筒 + 外框像空心竹子一样抵抗弯曲；: Supertall load paths: gravity accumulates downward, wind pushes sideways, and the core plus perimeter frame resists bending like a hollow tube. An opposing top damper reduces sway.
奥的斯发明钢缆断裂时自动卡住的安全装置，人们才敢乘电梯上高楼。: Otis’s automatic safety brake prevented a platform falling after rope failure, making people willing to ride elevators in tall buildings.
让人敢乘电梯的不是电机，而是**失效保护**：即使钢缆断了，轿厢也不能坠落。安全: Trust in elevators depends on **fail-safe protection**, not just a motor. A car must be stopped even after a suspension failure. A safety system uses excessive downward speed under [[p:gravity|gravity]] to trigger braking, replacing reliance on the cable alone with automatic protection.
轿厢通过钢缆绕过顶部曳引轮，另一端挂着配重，电机只需克服两者的重量差，因此很省电: A traction elevator’s cables pass over a driven sheave to a counterweight, so the motor mainly overcomes the load imbalance. An overspeed governor activates safety gear that grips the guide rails. Modern systems add multiple cables, buffers and computerized group dispatch.
1852 年美国机械师伊莱沙·奥的斯（Elisha Otis）发明安全制动装置；: American mechanic Elisha Otis invented a safety brake in 1852. At a New York exhibition in 1854, he stood on a platform and had its rope cut; the brake held it. A New York department store installed an early safety passenger elevator in 1857. Siemens demonstrated an electric elevator in 1880.
电梯让高层不再是\"阁楼\"而是最贵的楼层，城市从此向高空发展。: Elevators transformed upper floors from inconvenient attics into desirable, expensive space, allowing cities to grow upward.
不承重、挂在结构外的玻璃外墙，是现代写字楼的标志。: Non-load-bearing glass facades hang from structural frames and became a hallmark of modern offices.
外墙不再承重之后，就可以变成一层挂在结构外面的\"皮肤\"；玻璃透光，但也让热量: Once exterior walls no longer support the building, they can form a hanging skin. Glass admits light but also transfers heat, so curtain-wall design manages [[p:heat|heat transfer]] and [[p:optics|reflection and transmission]].
铝合金框架通过连接件挂在每层楼板边缘，框中镶嵌玻璃板，接缝用密封胶防水。现代幕墙: Aluminum frames attach to floor edges and hold sealed glass panels. Modern systems use insulating glass and low-emissivity coatings to admit visible light while limiting infrared heat transfer.
1952 年纽约利华大厦和 1958 年西格拉姆大厦把全玻璃幕墙变成现代写字楼的: New York’s Lever House (1952) and Seagram Building (1958) helped establish all-glass curtain walls as a modern-office symbol. The 1950s [[float-glass|float-glass process]] made large, flat panes affordable.
玻璃幕墙塑造了全球城市天际线；但炎热地区的全玻璃建筑空调能耗很高，反射光也可能造: Glass facades shaped skylines worldwide. In hot climates, fully glazed buildings can demand substantial cooling, and reflections can create glare.
在工厂预制墙板、楼板甚至整个房间模块，到现场像搭积木一样拼装。: Factory-made walls, floors and even complete rooms are assembled on site like building blocks.
工厂里有固定的工位、机器和质检，比工地上风吹日晒更适合精细作业；构件按统一模数生: Fixed workstations, machinery and quality checks support precision better than exposed construction sites. Standard dimensions allow interchangeable components and mass production ([[p:standard|standardization]], [[p:scale|economies of scale]]).
墙板、楼板、楼梯甚至带装修的整间房屋模块在工厂预制，运到现场用塔吊吊装，再连接节: Factories produce wall panels, slabs, stairs and sometimes fully finished rooms. Cranes place them on site, where joints are connected, grouted and linked to services. This shortens on-site schedules and reduces wet work and waste.
1851 年伦敦水晶宫用预制的铸铁和玻璃构件在约半年内建成。20 世纪初美国西尔: London’s Crystal Palace used prefabricated iron and glass components to rise in roughly six months in 1851. Sears sold kit homes by mail in the early twentieth century. In 2015, a Chinese company assembled a 57-story modular tower in Changsha in 19 days.
装配式建筑提高了质量和速度。难点在于运输限制、节点抗震和标准化与个性化的平衡。: Prefabrication improves speed and quality. Challenges include transport limits, earthquake-resistant connections and balancing standardization with individual design.
让建筑在地震中能变形耗能而不倒塌，隔震支座能把地面晃动与楼体隔开。: Ductile structures deform and dissipate earthquake energy without collapsing; isolation bearings separate much ground motion from the building.
地震时地面来回晃动，建筑因惯性想留在原地，于是受到巨大的水平力（[[p:newt: During an earthquake, moving ground acts on a building whose inertia resists motion ([[p:newton|Newton’s laws]]). Motion can amplify when seismic frequencies approach the building’s natural frequency ([[p:wave|resonance]]).
**抗震**的思路是让结构有足够的延性，大震时可以弯曲变形、吸收能量而不突然倒塌: **Earthquake resistance** provides ductility so structures bend and absorb energy without sudden collapse. **Base isolation** places layered-rubber bearings between building and foundation to reduce transmitted shaking. **Damping** adds devices that dissipate energy within the structure.
1970 年代新西兰工程师罗宾逊（Bill Robinson）发明了铅芯橡胶隔震: New Zealand engineer Bill Robinson invented lead-rubber isolation bearings in the 1970s. Japan adopted new seismic standards in 1981; buildings meeting them suffered markedly less damage in the 1995 Kobe earthquake.
抗震规范让地震多发国家的大城市能够安全地建造高楼，医院和应急中心尤其普遍采用隔震: Seismic codes support safer tall construction in earthquake-prone cities. Hospitals and emergency facilities frequently use base isolation.
在三维模型里集成建筑的所有构件和数据，设计、施工和运维共用一套模型。: A shared 3D model combines building components and information across design, construction and operation.
一栋楼可以先在计算机里\"盖\"一遍。把每根梁、每段管道都作为带属性的对象存进同: A building can first be assembled virtually. Beams and pipes become objects with properties in one model, from which drawings, quantities and schedules are derived—an application of [[p:abstraction|abstraction and layering]].
建筑、结构和机电各专业在共享的三维模型中协同设计，软件能自动发现\"风管撞上了梁: Architectural, structural and building-services teams coordinate in a shared 3D model. Software detects clashes such as ducts crossing beams. Time and cost data support construction sequencing, and the completed model supports owner operations.
1970 年代美国学者查尔斯·伊斯门（Charles Eastman）提出用计算: Charles Eastman proposed computer-based building descriptions in the 1970s. Products including ArchiCAD and, later, Revit developed this approach. From 2016, the UK required BIM for central-government projects.
BIM 减少了返工和变更，让复杂造型的建筑得以准确建造，也是建筑 [[digit: BIM reduces rework and supports accurate construction of complex forms. It also provides a foundation for building [[digital-twin|digital twins]].
挖掘机、塔吊、盾构机等用液压和钢铁放大人力，让大型工程快速完成。: Excavators, tower cranes and tunnel-boring machines use hydraulic power and steel to multiply human capability and accelerate construction.
用液压油传递压力，一个小泵就能推动大油缸产生几十吨的力（[[p:leverage: Hydraulic pressure lets a small pump drive a large cylinder with forces of tens of tons ([[p:leverage|mechanical advantage]], [[p:fluid|Pascal’s principle]]). Diesel engines or electric motors supply energy, allowing one machine to perform work once requiring many people.
**挖掘机**靠几组液压缸控制动臂、斗杆和铲斗；**塔式起重机**用平衡臂和配重: **Excavators** use hydraulic cylinders to move boom, stick and bucket. **Tower cranes** balance loads with counterweights and can climb with a building. **Bulldozers and rollers** prepare ground; tunnel-boring machines excavate underground (see [[tunnel-boring-machine]]).
